title: R110 pump-current shunt is fitted as 0.62 ohm (C25341) instead of 62 ohm
statement: R110 is the 62 ohm pump-current sense resistor across LSU_RT and LSU_IP, but its LCSC code C25341 (1206W4F620LT5E) is listed as 620 mOhm by both JLC and LCSC. The 62 ohm part of the same family is C17971 (620J). With 0.62 ohm the pump-current gain is about 1/100 of nominal, so lambda would stay near 1 and the wideband would not work. Also reported: [P17.01] R110 pump-current sense resistor is 0.62 ohm, not 62 ohm: R110 is meant to be 62 ohm (the mck1117 pump sense resistor, 61.9 ohm). The BOM places C25341 = 1206W4F620LT5E, which is 620 mohm. The Uniroyal code 'L' means x10^-3. The pump-current measurement is then about 100x too small and the wideband cannot work. The o | [P03.01] R110 pump sense resistor is 0.62 ohm, not 62 ohm (C25341): BOM part C25341 is UNI-ROYAL 1206W4F620LT5E. The 11th code L means x10^-3, so it is 620 mOhm. Firmware assumes 61.9 ohm x gain 10, so measured pump current is about 100x too small and lambda reads about 1.0 whatever the exhaust is. The Nernst loop still closes | [B16.01] R110 (wideband pump shunt, 62 ohm) built with LCSC C25341 = 0.62 ohm: Source and both fab BOMs fit R110 (62 ohm, 1206) as C25341. That is UNI-ROYAL 1206W4F620LT5E, 620 mohm. The Ip sense signal (U105 gain 10) is about 100x smaller than designed, roughly 8 ADC counts per mA instead of about 770, so lambda from the stock wideband
best_evidence: design.py:64 LCSC_R1206['62']; wideband.py:153; ordered and current fab_*jlcpcb_bom.csv '62,R110,R_1206_3216Metric,C25341'; kb/parts_manifest.json C25341 desc 620 mohm; tools/lcsc.py finds C17971 1206W4F620JT5E = 62 ohm. R110 sits between LSU_RT and LSU_IP (pcb_nets). Only value/LCSC mismatch in all 16 BOMs.
suggested_fix: Ordered boards: replace R110 by hand with a 62 ohm 1 % 1206 (C17971 1206W4F620JT5E, $0.0053) or a 61.9 / 62 ohm part. Current: change LCSC_R1206['62'] and wideband.py:153 to C17971. Add a script check of LCSC resistance against the schematic value.

title: Tach output wired straight to harness 2I on 1989-95 boards; 2I is an igniter input, no pull-up, firmware drives it
statement: Mazda workshop terminal-voltage tables for 1994 (Igniter) and 1995 (Ignition control module) list 2I as an Input to the PCME. The ordered 1994-95 motherboard rev 0.9 connects net OUT_TACH directly to J1.2I with no jumper, so a configured tach output would fight the igniter. Current rev 0.12/0.13 has JP5 (open), which is correct. Also reported: [R09.01] No pull-up on 2I for stock igniter (1989-95): The stock ECU supplies a pull-up on cavity 2I (igniter IGf/tach-related open-collector line). With the stock igniter driving 2I the two outputs contend. | [B17.02] Tach 2I hard-wired to OUT_TACH on 1989-93 and 1994-95, firmware default on: The ordered boards connect cavity 2I directly to the tach driver with no jumper, and the firmware sets tachOutputPin by default. The current design leaves it open by default (JP5, R3 | [F01.01] Ordered firmware drives tach output into 2I on 1989-95: The ordered firmware lacks miataNoTachOutput(), so the 1989-93 and 1994-95 presets leave tachOutputPin on PE3. The ordered 1989-95 motherboards wire OUT_TACH straight to 2I, which the FSM-based PIN notes show is the igniter signal INTO the ECU. The ECU will pu | [PIN-9495-B.01] 2I (tach/IGf) has no pull-up and no input on either 94-95 board: 2I is left floating on cur_mb8995 (JP5 open, R37 not fitted) and goes to MCU low-side Q14 with no pull-up on ord_mb9495; firmware assigns no tach output (miataNoTachOutput). If the 94-95 tachometer or igniter signal relies on an ECU pull-up on 2I, the needle r | [R12.05] Tach on 89-95 is a real field problem: Owners had no tach after an install: on a 95 (alarm tap on 2I, staff asked whether the wire is on 1F or 2I), and on 90-93 with R8 coils (a case jumper plus a 1 k resistor were needed). title: Ordered 1994-95 and 1989-93 boards: A/C request and clutch inputs active-low with no pull-up, polarity not set in firmware
statement: Mazda tables show 4F <1 V with A/C on, else B+, and 4I B+ released, <1 V depressed. rusEFI's own Hellen NB2 uses acSwitchMode=PI_PULLUP and clutchDownPinMode=PI_INVERTED_DEFAULT. This board has the 22k/10k divider to ground with R21/R22 not fitted, and the preset sets no pin mode, so both inputs read 0 V always: A/C compressor never commanded. Fitting R21 without inverting the mode inverts the request. Also reported: [F01.02] A/C switch input polarity never set (reads active-high): The firmware never sets acSwitchMode, so rusEFI treats a HIGH pin as an A/C request. R16 (a secondary FSM voltage table) says 1989-93 pin 1Q is below 2.5 V when A/C is on (active-low), and the 1989-95 motherboard pulls the pin up to VBAT. With A/C off the ECU  | [PIN-9900-A.05] A/C request input 1P: level and polarity not established, no pull-up: No source gives the electrical character of 1P (12 V active, or open collector to ground). Firmware does not set acSwitch polarity or pull; the R21 pull-up is not fitted. If the stock A/C amplifier switches to ground, the A/C request is never seen.
best_evidence: miata_board.cpp setInputs() has no acSwitchMode; rusEFI hw_layer/debounce.cpp:109-115 (inverts only for PI_PULLUP); kb/research/R16 (1Q); cur_mb8995 R21 4.7k to VBAT_IN; PIN-9900 row 1P (cannot verify)
suggested_fix: Fit R21 and R22 by hand on the ordered NB2 board before use; in the NB2 presets set acSwitchMode=PI_PULLUP-equivalent (active low) and clutchDownPinMode inverted; document in INSTALL.md.

title: 1990-93 fuel pump 2T unconnected and F/P wiring advice
statement: On the 1991 NA6 ECU pin 2T carries no wire. The pump runs from the circuit-opening relay, switched by the vane AFM fuel-pump contact and the starter signal, not by the ECU. README lists 2T as 'fuel pump relay' for 1989-95. If the vane AFM is removed (speed-density, the board's premise) the pump will not run unless the AFM-plug pump contact is bridged or rewired. Also reported: [B14.08] 1990-93 fuel pump F/P wiring advice not verifiable here: The advice (stock harness has no wire in 2T, so add one from the diagnosis box F/P terminal to 2T; bridging F/P to GND runs the pump) is sourced from third-party guides. The design side is correct (2T = OUT_FP relay-driver). The statement that the pump is swit
best_evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2: CONN#2 T has no wire; AFM terminals A(LT GRN)/B(BLK) 'FUEL PUMP SW' go to the circuit opening relay; ST SIGN FUSE VIO. rusEFI 1990 table: 3T '*'. README table row 2T.
suggested_fix: Document in INSTALL/README that 1989-93 pump is not ECU-controlled; give a bypass instruction (relay or jumper) for AFM deletion; optionally a header to re-wire the circuit-opening relay to OUT_FP. Read 1990/1992/1993 diagrams to confirm 2T is empty all years.

title: Ordered 4-layer daughterboard has hundreds of vias inside SMD pads, with fill unspecified
statement: About 25 open 0.3 mm holes lie in each 37 mm2 tab (664 vias in same-net pads board-wide). README says order epoxy-filled and capped, but the gbrjob/drill files carry no fill information, the repo has no order record, and JLC fill is free only at 6+ layers. Open holes (2.8 mm3 per tab) can swallow about the same volume as the paste on the tab (~2 mm3, stencil thickness assumed), giving voided or starved tab joints and higher Rth. Reflow solder wicks away from  | [B04.01] Via-in-pad is on ~300 ordinary pads, not only DPAK tabs and TVSs: 719 of 1349 via holes (0.3 mm, open to the pad mask opening) touch SMD pad copper; about 300 are in non-thermal pads, while README 'Before ordering' item 9 names only DPAK tabs and clamp TVS pads. Unfilled they wick solder and cause tombstoning and starved joi
conflict: Via-in-pad counts differ: about 620 of 1423 (B08.01), 664 of 1423 (B03.01/B18.05), 373 in DPAK tabs plus about 350 elsewhere (B04.02), and 719 of 1349 on the current 6-layer (B04.01). Likely different counting rules.

title: 99-00 alternator overcharge from ground offset
statement: Owners report battery voltage rising to 16 V or more and a boiling battery on 99-00 MSPNP2. The vendor engineer, relayed second-hand, blames a ground offset between the alternator body and battery negative that latches the field on. The fix given is a ground strap from alternator body to chassis. Lean stalls were also traced to the base map's battery-voltage correction.
best_evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/id1050x-battery-voltage-correction-factor-alternator-overcharging-99-00-mspnp2-107805/ ; https://www.miataturbo.net/mspnp-55/99-mspnp2-blown-up-battery-voltage-regulation-issues-103610/
suggested_fix: Ship alternator control off by default (the repo already does). Add the ground-strap instruction and a voltage-correction note to the install guide. Consider a firmware over-voltage cutoff.

title: Automatic-transmission cars: A/T lines (1R, 1T, 4Y, 1I, 1N, 1V, 3L) unserved and store says swapped autos covered
statement: The FAQ says cars swapped from automatic to manual are covered and every product 'Fits' row says 'manual and manual-swapped', while the README says automatic cars are untested with transmission signals unconnected, Mazdaspeed unsupported, no immobiliser/OBD-II/EGR/purge/VTCS. None of this is on a product page. Also reported: [PIN-8993-A.04] 1V clutch input reads constant 12 V on automatics; firmware assigns clutchDownPin on every year: On M/T cars 1V is BRN-WHT to the clutch switch (to ground, shared with the cruise unit). On A/T cars the same pin is BLK-BLU from the ignition switch, i.e. 12 V with key on, so an automatic would read 'clutch down' permanently. On M/T the ground-switched line  | [PIN-9495-B.08] Automatic 94-95 transmission lines 1I/1N/1V not served: On automatics 1I, 1N, 1V connect to the transmission PCM and the ECU reads the park/neutral switch; board leaves 1I/1N open and treats 1V as a clutch input. Shift quality or limp mode possible. Repo already lists automatics as untested. | [PIN-9697-B.08] Automatic transmission lines not connected: 1R GRN, 1T GRN/BLU and 4Y BLU/YEL are PCM-to-TCM lines (content unverified) and are open. 1L carries an A/T signal that the board reads as a clutch switch. statement: If the MAP sensor is invalid, speed density uses mapEstimateTable which rusEFI defaults to a flat 60 kPa and the presets do not change. title: VE tables are invented or reused (NB flat 80 percent above 116 kPa, 1.6 L VE reused)
statement: All NB VE rows from 116 to 220 kPa are 80 (invented fill, README says 'about 100 kPa'). title: 5 V rail not measured; ADC reference independent of sensor supply
statement: The F407 ADC reference is VDDA from the +3V3 LDO (+-2 % at 25 C, +-3 % over temperature) while MAP/TPS/CLT/IAT are fed from the +5V buck (about 4.88-5.12 V, per P05). rusEFI assumes exactly 3.3 V and 5 V and has no VREFINT or rail compensation here. Worst-corner MAP error is about +-7 kPa at 100 kPa and +-13 kPa at 200 kPa; CLT/IAT about +-2 K at 25-80 C and +-7 K at -20 C. Typical error is about half. Also reported: [P07.02] No ADC channel measures any 5 V rail; static rail tolerance +-6.7 % worst: No ADC input monitors +5V/V5_SENS/V5_EXT (inputs are KNOCK,TPS,MAP,CLT,IAT,AFR,AUX1-3,VBATT,VIGN), so firmware cannot correct. Gain error between independently toleranced rails: 5 V = 5.0 V +-3.7 % (LMR14020 VFB +-2 % + 1 % dividers), 3V3 +-3 % (LDL1117) = +-6 | [P07.01] Sensor readings scale with the +5V sag; ADC reference is the 3.3 V LDO: V5_SENS/V5_EXT follow +5V (tracker +-5 mV) while the ADC reference stays 3.3 V (LDL1117 holds to about 3.7 V in), so MAP/TPS/AFM/CLT/IAT read low by 1-V5/5: -21.8 % at the repo's level II crank value of 3.91 V, -10 % at 4.5 V, -5 % at 4.75 V (MPX5700AP spec'd
best_evidence: datasheets/txt/C435835_LDL1117S33R.txt VOUT accuracy +-2 %/+-3 %; kb/parts/P05 Vout 4.88-5.12; miata_board.cpp:30,64-72 (adcVcc 3.3, MPX Vout=5 V x ...); adc_inputs.cpp:57 (only a +-10 % diagnostic); computed r = (V5/5)/(V3/3.3) = 1.056 worst
suggested_fix: Tune baro/offset at key-on and accept, or pull CLT/IAT up to +3V3 so they are ratiometric to VDDA. For MAP, calibrate the gain on the bench or add a firmware VREFINT/5V correction.

title: Thermal model assumptions (h=10, no ambient) unproven
statement: Board mean rise is ~P/(2*0.0095 m2*h), so it scales with 1/h. In a closed metal case the board loses heat with gap conduction (~1.7 W/m2K) plus weak radiation to bare metal, so h is likely 3-5, not 10. The repo also gives the rise only 'above the air around the board', and the case-to-cabin rise under carpet (~10-20 K) is missing. Allowable air around the board for the MCU (105 C junction) at sustained 7200 rpm falls from the repo's 65-73 C to ~54 C (with pin conduction) or ~34 C (without), before adding the case rise. Also reported: [F05.09] board_thermal.py: assumed loads, no ambient, uncertain h; needs undocumented tools: Loss table is hard-coded (1.2 A at 80% duty per injector, rail loads guessed), h=10 W/m2K (stated to be good only to a factor of 1.5), Rth_jc from maker figures, laminate k recalled. No case-air offset. Self-test gives 54 C/W at h=10 against 'recalled 40-50'.  | [B15.05] All temperature margins are model output with an assumed h = 10 W/m2K and an undefined case air: Every temperature rests on both faces cooled at 10 W/m2K to 'air around the board'. The self-test comparison with datasheet RthJA is 'as recalled, not re-read'. Inside a closed stock ECU case, natural convection plus radiation is plausibly 3-8 W/m2K, and the c
best_evidence: Reran repo script on the board file: h=10 seq 31 C mean, MCU +40 (matches repo); h=5 no pins 63 C mean, MCU +71, TVS +83; h=5 with pins 41 C mean, MCU +51, TVS +61; h=3 no pins 104 C mean. h and case rise are my assumptions (unverified).
suggested_fix: Re-run the model with h=4-5 per face plus a case-to-cabin conductance; state the limit as cabin temperature; measure a built board in the actual case at ~3 W and ~6 W.

title: Ordered 1989-93 motherboard pairs two injector drivers per wire (R23/R24); thin margin at 20 mH
statement: Two injectors in parallel on one wire draw about 2.04 A at 14.4 V. At L=20 mH each (10 mH combined), ST's repetitive 125 C curve allows 2.2 A, so there is essentially no margin if the driver's own clamp took the energy (30.7 mJ per event, 1.84 W at 7200 rpm batch). The external clamp is what makes this case viable. Keep D42/D43/D46/D47 on 1989-93, and do not make them DNP on that year. Also reported: [B03.05] 1989-93 ordered mb: R23/R24 fitted pairs two drivers per injector wire: R23 and R24 are populated by default, so INJ1||INJ4 drive 2U and INJ2||INJ3 drive 2V. The repo's current decision is one driver per wire. Two paralleled drivers do not share the turn-off clamp energy evenly, so the first-off driver or TVS takes it.
best_evidence: pcb_footprints (R23/R24 have LCSC); VERIFICATION.md 'one driver per injector wire'; audit A11
suggested_fix: Remove R23 and R24. INJ1 then drives 2U and INJ2 drives 2V, with no firmware change. Keep D3/D4. For sequential, fit R25/R26 instead, and never R26 on an automatic.

title: Wideband F1 heater PTC derates below warm-up current in a hot case
statement: Repo says F1 holds about 2.4 A at 60 C. Datasheet table gives 1.99 A at 60 C, 1.79 A at 70 C, 1.34 A at 85 C. rusEFI warm-up ramp starts at 7 V effective, so a 2.5 ohm cold heater draws about 2.8 A rms, above hold from about 45 C ambient and above the scaled trip current (about 2.2 A) at 85 C. A hot-soaked ECU may trip F1 and the wideband times out (60 s). Also reported: [P04.01] F1 PTC may nuisance-trip at ramp start in hot ECU case: At ramp start (7 V effective, cold heater about 3.2 ohm, 14.4 V supply) heater RMS current is about 2.2 A. F1 hold derates to 1.99 A at 60 C and 1.34 A at 85 C, so at 85 C case air (trip about 2.2 A scaled) a cold-sensor warm-up can trip F1. The wideband then
best_evidence: datasheets/txt/C22446884 derating row 2920L300: 4.53/4.02/3.51/3.00/2.52/2.26/1.99/1.79/1.34; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/heater_control.cpp:109,173-176; Bosch LSU49 heater 7.5 W; cold 2.5 ohm is the repo's own figure (unverified). Trip scaling is inferred.
suggested_fix: Use 2920L400/30GR (4 A hold, 1.79 A at 85 C) or 2920L500/30GR; check the harness wire and the JST 3 A contact. Or start the ramp at lower V/longer time when the F1 area is hot. Measure heater R and case temperature on the first build.

title: Clutch switch inputs (1L, 3I) are switch-to-ground and pull-ups R20-R22 are not fitted
statement: FSM shows 1L BRN/WHT to clutch/neutral/cruise switches (A/T: TCM) and 1M GRN/RED VSS from the cluster-mounted sensor shared with TCM and cruise, but not whether they are 12 V-driven or ground/open-collector. If open-collector, no pulses without fitting R20/R22; effect: no VSS-based features, clutch never seen. Also reported: [PIN-9900-B.02] Clutch switch (3I) is switched to ground; R22 not fitted: Mazda diagram shows 3I BR/W going to the clutch switch (B1-21) whose other terminal is a B (ground) wire, so the input is a switch to ground. The 1999-2000 README says these inputs are 12 V driven and ships R22 unfitted, so the input floats and the clutch is n
best_evidence: Mazda 2000 wiring pdf p.25 (B-1c: clutch switch B1-21, BR/W and B(E)); motherboards/1999-2000/README.md:130; parts_list R22 'NOT FITTED'
suggested_fix: Fit R22 by default on 1999-2000 (and tell the buyer); keep R21 (A/C) unfitted. Check polarity (clutchDownPin inverted?) in firmware.

title: 1996-2005 tach (3O) is open-collector with no pull-up while Hellen drives push-pull 12 V
statement: The stock 3O waveform runs from 0 V to about 12 V (6 div at 2 V/div) at 2 pulses per rev, and rusEFI's Proteus/Hellen pin maps list 3O as a HIGH-SIDE output. The board drives 3O with a ZXMS6004 low side and has no pull-up on the motherboard. If the cluster does not supply its own pull-up the tach stays at zero. Nobody has measured the unplugged-ECU level. Also reported: [R30.04] 1996-2005 tach and alternator: project open-collector without pull-up, Hellen drives push-pull 12 V: Hellen NA8/NB1/NB2 drive the tach from PP2 and the NB alternator from PP1 (TC4427 push-pull on +12V_PROT). The project uses open-collector low sides and only the 1989-95 board has a 1k pull-up (R37). If the cluster or regulator input does not idle high, the ta
best_evidence: charm.li 2002 oscilloscope image 1009477327 (Y5J3940W122), 3O to 4A, 2 V/div; rusEFI Proteus-NB2 page ('3O Tach High-Side 1'); interconnect.md cur_mb0105: 3O=OUT_TACH->JD1.11 only; no tach pull-up documented for NB2 in VERIFICATION/INSTALL.
suggested_fix: Add a car test: key on with ECU unplugged, measure 3O (about 12 V means a pull-up exists, 0 V means the ECU must source). Pre-fit a DNP pull-up pad (about 1-4.7k to 4AF) or a high-side option.

title: 1999-2000 pin table conflicts: 1U/3Q usage and VICS solenoid left de-energised
statement: 3Q is wired (verified W/L VICS valve B1-10, low side) but NB1 firmware sets no output; README says only 'not set up'. A forum report (unverified) says the stock solenoid is energised below about 5200 rpm and springs open above it, so a never-energised valve would leave VICS in the high-rpm state at all speeds, costing low and mid torque. No damage. Also reported: [R30.05] Pin-table conflicts on 1999-2000: 1U and 3Q: rusEFI's NB1 table and netlist put VICS on 3Q and VVT on 4E, and the front O2 heater on 1U; the project maps 1U to a VVT output and 3Q to the main-relay output (J5.5). One of the two tables is wrong; a wrong output on a heater or VICS wire could matter.
best_evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/.../hellenMiataNB1/connectors/main.yaml; nb1_nets.txt /OUT_VICS P2.47(3Q), /OUT_VVT P2.67(4E); kb/interconnect.md lines 576-656
suggested_fix: Check against the 1999-2000 Miata wiring diagram before first power-up; leave the cavities unconnected until confirmed.

title: F2/F3 PTC (SMD1812-200-30) derates below VVT/IAC coil current when hot
statement: The 2002 FSM gives the OCV coil as 6.9-7.9 ohm at 20 C, so peak current at 14.4 V is 1.8-2.1 A. F3 is a 2 A hold PTC that derates to about 1.45 A at 60 C and 0.8 A at 85 C. At high VVT duty in a hot cabin it can trip, and the valve then falls back to full retard (lost top-end torque, no damage). Also reported: [B12.03] F3/F2 PTC derates below VVT/IAC valve current when hot: F2/F3 are SMD1812-200-30 (hold 2.0 A at 25 C, 1.45 A at 60 C, 0.80 A at 85 C, trip 4 A). A VVT valve of 6.9-7.9 ohm (later-Mazda spec; NB value unverified) draws 1.8-2.1 A at 14.4 V DC, about 1.1 A rms at 50 % duty, so a hot case can nuisance-trip the fuse and
best_evidence: charm.li 2002 'Oil Control Valve Inspection' image 757208362 (6.9-7.9 ohm at 20 C); derating table is from kb/parts/P16-ptc-fuses.md (datasheet C46641168), not re-read; 14.4/6.9=2.09 A; firmware auxPid maxValue 90 (miata_board.cpp:294). FSM OCV scope shows about 40 % high at idle.
suggested_fix: Use a higher-hold part for F3 (and check F2), or a larger-footprint PTC or 3 A fuse. Cap VVT duty or accept the trip as fail-safe; the A-audit's 7.5 ohm assumption is now confirmed as spec.

title: AEM 30-3427 connector identity and JST pin-1 end not document-verified
statement: AEM manuals give the 8-way pin/colour table (VERIFIED) but the JST SPUD-001T-P0.5 sentence appears under the wiring notes next to the 10-way Power/IO connector; the 30-0302 manual (only connector A) repeats it for connector A. No source read names the 8-way sensor connector's housing, so J2 = PUD for 30-3427 is only inferred. AEM's page was unreadable (403). Also reported: [P21.02] Circuit-1 end of the JST row and AEM=JST numbering not document-verified: JST catalog drawing verifies pitch, row of pin 1 relative to the boss (pin 2 +7.7 mm to boss matches PCB) but not which end of the row is circuit 1; AEM does not state its numbers are JST's. The mapping rests on an owner photo. A flip puts sense wires on wrong
best_evidence: kb/research/files/R15/aem_30-0300_fae.txt lines 105-113; AEM 30-0302 manual (read, not kept) 'optional extras' beside Connector A; web search for PUDP-08V-S + AEM found nothing
suggested_fix: Plug one real 30-3427 into a sample J2 (or into an S08B-PUDSS-1 header) before claiming fit; otherwise ship or specify a seller-made pigtail with PUDP-08V-S.

title: Boost ignition tables aggressive for 91 octane and public NB maps disagree by 18 degrees
statement: The rusEFI NB ignition table (used by the repo for NB1 and NB2) has 28 deg at 99.5 kPa, 4144-4884 rpm, and 30-31 deg at 6800-8000 rpm. Speeduino's NB8B PNP tune has only 11 deg at 96 kPa, 4700-5200 rpm, and 9 deg at 7200 rpm. The Speeduino NA PNP tunes have 29 deg. None of them states test conditions. Also reported: [F02.04] NA/NB boost ignition rows still aggressive for 91 octane: NA table gives 22 deg at 2300 rpm and 18-21 deg at 3900-8000 rpm at 160 kPa (8.7 psi); NB gives 24-25 deg at 6800-8000 rpm at 158 kPa. Combined with untuned fuel this is unsafe on pump gas. Only forum rules of thumb (about 1 deg/psi pull) were found as compari
best_evidence: Computed from files/R14/rusefi_src/mazda_miata_vvt.cpp (mapBased18vvtTimingTable) and files/R14/speeduino_tunes/NB8B PNP base tune.msq (advTable1); notes section 5.1
suggested_fix: Tell users the base map is a starting point, with the first WOT pulls only after wideband and knock checks. Consider a more conservative shipped table above 80 kPa for the first start.

title: Battery sense taken after D7 and F1 reads low
statement: R11.1 is on net +12V (F1.2/L1.1/D12), after SS34 and the PTC, so VBATT reads about 0.4-0.8 V low and load dependent. Also reported: [B03.08] Ordered battery sense taken after D7 and F1: R11 sits on the +12V net with F1.2, behind D7 and F1, so VBAT reads about 0.4-0.6 V low and load dependent.
suggested_fix: Optional: move R11 pin 1 to VBAT_IN, for example J1 pin 1 or D7 pad 2. Or accept it and apply a firmware trim.

title: Hall 1k pull-up needs 4.7 mA sink; hall input field instability
statement: Three independent users report rpm spikes and unstable running above about 5000 rpm in full sequential on Miatas with Speeduino boards. A vendor traced it to noisy unshielded Hall CKP/CMP wiring and fixed it with a Schmitt-trigger input stage. His first inverting circuit made starting hard until the trigger edge setting was changed. This project's Hall inputs are a plain RC plus the STM32 pin's own hysteresis, the same class as Speeduino's. Root cause is not proven, because Speeduino developers could not reproduce it on the bench. Also reported: [P13.02] Hall 1k pull-up needs about 4.7 mA sensor sink; sink capability unverified: Each hall input pulls up through 1k from V5_EXT (minus D35 drop), so the sensor must sink about 4.7 mA with Vol below the STM32 production-tested VIL of 0.99 V. Neither the NA optical CAS nor the NB BP4W sensor datasheet was found; Hellen uses 4.7k pull-ups.
best_evidence: speeduino.com/forum/viewtopic.php?t=6281 (pages 1-2, posts 2024-03 to 2025-12); repo/scripts/design.py:433-446; Speeduino NA6 v1.3 nets CRANK-IN/CAM-IN (R33-R36, C15, C16)
suggested_fix: Reserve pads or a footprint for an optional 74HCT14 or comparator stage on HALL1/HALL2, or plan a first-bench test with logged tooth-log noise. Ship with a documented trigger filter setting.

title: TC4427 and low-side driver field failures killed MCU pins
statement: In Nov 2021 an NB2 and a Frankenso/NB1 lost MCU pins behind the 12 V TC4427 (8-10 ohm to ground, 2-20 ohm to 3.3 V). Fix: 100 ohm series + Schottky (output-0.3); NB1 also needed R23 1k removed for alternator charging (17-18 V ramps); OEM Miata alternator wire uses 1k + 100 nF. This project already has 100 ohm + B5819W; alternator ships off, which is prudent. Also reported: [R31.05] Low-side output driver failures: backfeed, shorts and second sources: The ULN2003 does not survive a short to +12 V (hellen-one #360). The alternator push-pull output fed energy back into MCU pins on the NB2, and the series 1k added as the fix later stopped the alternator charging. A ZXMS6005 substitute for the AUIPS2041 was not
best_evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/360 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/23 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB1-issues/issues/29 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/34 ; /20
suggested_fix: Keep alternator control off by default. Do not add series R on a field line without a charging test. Forbid substitute driver parts at JLCPCB. Test every output for back-feed on the key-off state.

title: Pinned rusEFI is 239 commits behind master with no bump workflow
statement: Pin is dated 2026-10-30; master is 239 commits ahead 17 days later. There is no scheduled bump workflow (fw-custom-example has a daily one). Each bump needs re-running pin checks, image checks, simulations and ideally a car test. Pin to a release/LTS ref (the action supports branches named lts*).
best_evidence: git log in submodule; GitHub compare API 1374bd07...master ahead_by 239 (2026-11-16); custom-board-build/action.yaml 'lts' handling; Custom-Firmware wiki
suggested_fix: Freeze a customer-release commit, bump on a schedule, record it in release notes.

title: Injector dead time has no primary source; public tables differ up to 2x
statement: rusEFI's NB lag table (the repo's) is 1.5 ms at 12 V and 1.25 ms at 14 V. FOME's is 1.04 ms at 12.8 V and 0.90 ms at 14.4 V. Speeduino uses 1.0 ms open time with about 100 % at 13.9 V. I found no Denso or Mazda dead-time or flow-at-pressure datasheet for 195500-1970, -2180, -3310 or -4060.
best_evidence: files/R14/rusefi_src and fome_src mazda_miata_vvt.cpp; Speeduino msq injOpen/injBatRates; notes section 2
suggested_fix: State in the install and tuning guide that dead time is a community estimate. Give a wideband-at-idle correction procedure and avoid presenting the table as measured.

title: No independent accuracy validation of FOME/rusEFI wideband
statement: The only documented accuracy is Bosch's sensor figure (+-0.007 at lambda 1, +-0.01 at 0.8, +-0.05 at 1.7). Firmware author comments claim 0.5% fit to the Bosch table. Forum validation was free air and a lighter flame only. No bottled-gas or side-by-side comparison was found.
best_evidence: Bosch ds lines 74-76 (kb/research/files/R15); lambda_conversion.cpp comments; forum t=1856 p.6 summary
suggested_fix: Run the bench plan in the notes, section 10, on the first boards and publish the results.

title: Igniter input level and threshold unknown; 100 ohm plus Schottky may eat margin
statement: The high level at the igniter is 5 V minus about 0.3-0.4 V (Schottky) minus I*100 ohm, with R144 3.3k (about 1.4 mA) also loading it. No source for the stock NA igniter or NB coil input current and threshold was found. If an igniter input needs more than a few mA, or about 3.5 V or more, the stage may not fire it. Hellen drives these inputs directly (4245A plus 10 ohm).
best_evidence: ext/hellen-one/modules/ign8/0.2/ign8-BOM.csv; web search found no numbers; design.py:297-335
suggested_fix: Before first run, measure the high level on the real stock coil pack and igniter with a scope (loaded). If the level is short, reduce R15-18 to 47 ohm. Check the 1206 dissipation first (see the R15-18 finding below).

title: MAP error band +-17.5 kPa at idle
statement: Datasheet accuracy +-2.5 %VFSS (VFSS 4.5 V, 6.43 mV/kPa) = +-0.1125 V = +-17.5 kPa over 0-85 C: +-50 % of a 35 kPa idle reading and +-17.6 % at 100 kPa. The absolute offset spec 0.184-0.409 V alone spans the whole budget. NXP gives no typical figure. A tune on one car absorbs the fixed part, but a shipped base map and temperature drift are exposed. Outside 0-85 C no accuracy is specified.
best_evidence: datasheets/C90152_MPX5700AP.pdf Table 1 p.2 (accuracy, Voff, sensitivity); MPX4250A Rev 8 Table 2 for comparison; computed.
suggested_fix: For NA cars offer MPX4250AP (+-3.5 kPa) or a 400 kPa SMD sensor. Enable the 'read MAP at start-up as baro' option (rusefi_config.txt:1242). Keep closed-loop lambda trim range wide on the base tune.

title: JLC assembly problems seen on Hellen boards
statement: On a Hellen NA6 rev B, a wideband analog input read 0 V from a poor resistor joint plus a flux blob on an MCU pin. JLC queried diode polarity during production. An NB2 was built with LMV324 instead of MCP6004. Only the polarity queries relate to rotation. I found no public rotated-part failure for these boards.
best_evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/hellenNA6_issues/issues/29 ; /23 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/4
suggested_fix: Check the JLC placement preview, inspect the first article for flux and joints, allow no substitutions, and test every analog input against a known voltage.

title: Load-dump crowbar on H72 failed short at 22 V
statement: A reporter ramped a bench supply on an h72b and heard a pop at about 22 V. The fault measured 0.5-0.7 ohm. The TVS was fine, and removing the crowbar MOSFETs cleared the short. The maintainer said the power12 module is the same on B and C. Hellen documents more than 24 V may damage the module.
best_evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/47 ; /121
suggested_fix: Bench-test the 24 V jump-start and 35 V load-dump cases with current limiting on a first article. Resolve the documented open item on PTC fuse ratings of 24-33 V.

title: Cold-crank brown-out limits
statement: The ISO 16750-2 starting profile has four levels. Level III (aged battery, cold) dips to 3 V for 15 ms and holds 5 V. Level II dips to 4.5 V and holds 6.5 V. Each level has a minimum functional status.
suggested_fix: Check the buck's drop-out and holdup (bulk C) against 6 V continuous and a 15 ms dip to 3-4.5 V; confirm the MCU does not reset or glitch the injectors.

title: Buck output capacitance below TI 47 uF stability note
statement: TI states 'for stability consideration, one 47 uF output capacitor is needed at least' for the 1 MHz / 5.5 uH example. The board has 3 x 10 uF at the buck output plus C26, which is about 25-30 uF after DC-bias derating (derating UNVERIFIED), at 2.3 MHz / 10 uH. The datasheet gives no formula to scale 47 uF to other fSW and L, so stability is not provable from the datasheet.
best_evidence: SNVSAA5B p.19 section 7.2.2.4; design.py:239-241; Samsung CL21A106KAYNNNE is X5R 25 V 0805 (C15850)
suggested_fix: Bench-measure load-step and Bode on the first board. Cheap hedge: swap C22/C23 for 22 uF 10 V 0805 X5R parts, or add one more 10 uF, to reach at least 47 uF nominal.

title: LDL1117 at or above 125 C Tj at 85 C air
statement: (5.0-3.3 V) x 0.2 A = 0.34 W and with theta-JA 120 K/W gives Tj about 126 C at 85 C air. At the repo's peak 0.3 A (SD writes) it is about 146 C, and 0.35 A is about 157 C, above the 150 C abs max. The tab has only one 0.3 mm via and a short trace as copper, so a real theta-JA at or above ST's 120 is likely.
best_evidence: LDL1117 Table 2/3 (Tj op 125, max 150, thetaJA 120); P05 3d load budget 0.2/0.3-0.35 A; vias.py: single +3V3 via at (134.5,93.25); layer crops u4_F_Cu.png
suggested_fix: Add a +3V3 copper area plus 4-6 vias under and around the U4 tab (free on the current rev); check the real 3.3 V current on the bench at 85 C.

title: Long dwell at sync loss open upstream
statement: uaEFI shows 150-460 ms dwell at sync loss while cranking. rusEFI discussions say an oscillator or PLL failure can leave ignition outputs stuck active. Proposed cures include CSS, a hardware watchdog and an MC33810 ignition IC. Two smoke incidents were reported. One was an M73 board with hardware damage and one an IGBT set on fire. Causes were not established.
best_evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/6349 ; /5730 ; /5728 ; /5729 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=48645
suggested_fix: First-article test: short the oscillator and check ignition pins go low. Check the pinned firmware for a dwell cap and CSS. Use a spare coil or igniter at first start.

title: ECU is sole radiator-fan control on 94-95
statement: Fan relay coil is fed from the ENGINE fuse and grounded only by ECU 1L; no thermoswitch. Preset turns radiator fan on at 100 C (off 96) and condenser fan at 95/91; stock values not found. Wrong/disabled fan config overheats the car.
best_evidence: FSM 1994 wiring p.10 Fig.5; rusEFI mazda_miata_1_6.cpp:282-285
suggested_fix: Document that fan must be verified in the tune; consider lower default (about 90-95 C) and a fail-on rule.

title: Stock functions silently absent (purge, EGR, PRC, rear heater)
statement: The FSM shows low-side ECU outputs for purge (YEL/RED), EGR vent (YEL), EGR vacuum (YEL/WHT), PRC solenoid (YEL/GRN) and rear HO2S heater (VIO), plus EGR boost/position inputs 3H/3J; none connected. Purge and EGR stay de-energised (safe). PRC is new (README lists 4J as unknown): possible hot-restart effect is UNVERIFIED.
best_evidence: 1997 wiring PDF p.16 solenoids at bottom; motherboards/1996-97/README.md 'Not connected'
suggested_fix: Document 4T/4O/4P/4J/4Z functions and their consequence; optionally expose 4T purge and 4Z rear heater on spare drivers.

title: IAC 2P/2Q both PCM terminals
statement: Mitchell lists 2P 'IAC (positive)' and 2Q 'IAC (negative)' with the scope measured between them; the repo and rusEFI wiki treat 2P as +12 V supply and 2Q as the low-side. Which one holds is not settled by the documents; coil resistance and drive frequency are not found for 1999-2005.
best_evidence: Mitchell 2005 lines 1254-1263, 2259-2263; mb_nb2.py:47; rusEFI wiki Miata 2002
suggested_fix: Measure 2P at key-on with the harness connected to a stock ECU before first power-up; fall back to a documented jumper if it is switched.

title: Vane AFM output level conflict between manuals
statement: 1990 manual voltages (via R16) are 3.8 V key on and 3.3 V idle; the 1994 and 1996 manuals give below 1 V key on and 1.0-2.0 V at idle. Lakey's measurements follow the 1990 direction. Either the meter polarity changed or a transcription is wrong; the VAF input scaling cannot be confirmed from documents alone.
best_evidence: wm1990 OCR/R16 terminal table vs CHARM 1994 'Air Flow Meter/Sensor' and CHARM 1996 spec pages
suggested_fix: Measure a real meter on a 1989-93 and a 1994-97 car before the next order; check the input divider and clamp against 0-5 V full range.

title: Header C2977586 plating unspecified
statement: Zhouri sheet says 'Au or Over Ni' and LCSC lists no plating, while socket is gold over nickel. A tin or unknown header against gold sockets risks fretting on sub-mA sensor lines, the problem the repo says it fixed.
best_evidence: datasheets/C2977586 p.1; lcsc.py params Contact Plating '-'; C124412 sheet 'Gold Over Nickel'; VERIFICATION.md:670
suggested_fix: Confirm plating by sample or supplier, or switch to a header with stated gold plating (e.g. C2337 listed Gold; its datasheet not read).

title: Renode firmware-in-loop does not test board wiring
statement: Stimulus is ideal voltages at named MCU pins using divider constants hard-coded in run_ecu.py, and the LSU plant uses the firmware's own scale factors, so a wrong divider, pin or connector on the PCB would not be seen. Many peripherals (ADC, DMA, NVIC, F103 ROM bootloader) are the authors' own models. The workflow runs only on workflow_dispatch, yet VERIFICATION.md:594 calls it 'in CI'. Not run here (no Renode).
best_evidence: sim.yaml on: workflow_dispatch; LsuSensor.cs header comment; sim/README.md gaps table
suggested_fix: Treat a pass as 'firmware config is self-consistent'. Confirm with a hardware-in-the-loop trigger/sensor rig on the real board.

title: Netlist checks compare design.py against itself
statement: Both sides come from the same Python source, so these checks catch generator bugs (split or merged nets) but not wrong pin numbering vs the real part or design errors. The only independent pin reference is check_mcu_pins vs ST XML, and it covers the F407 only. With no human schematic review, 'schematic matches design' is weak evidence.
best_evidence: check_sch_netlist.py:15-20 (exp from design.parts); gen_sch.py generates the schematic
suggested_fix: Add datasheet-derived pin tables (kb pinouts) as an independent check for each IC, and manually review pin 1 and orientation on the ordered boards.

title: Cheaper injector drivers and optional external clamp (NCV8401B, NCV8403A, ZXMS6005, AO3400A, SMBJ14A)
statement: NCV8403ASTT1G (SOT-223): 76 mohm max (135 hot) at 5 V, limit 10-20 A, 42 V clamp, EAS 470 mJ, Vth 1.0-2.2 V, $0.7396 at 30 and $0.6283 at 100, stock 1908. Fig. 8 typical curve shows about 80 mohm (25 C) and 130 mohm (150 C) at VGS = 3 V, so a 3.3 V GPIO can probably drive it and U11 could be deleted. Total is $11.14 at 30 against $22.11, saving about $11 per board. 3.3 V operation is typical-curve only, not guaranteed. Also reported: [R06.02] Bare AO3400A injector low-side is used by Blitzbox, unproven for flyback: Blitzbox drives high-impedance injectors with a bare AO3400A (30 V, SOT-23, 4k7 gate, 100k pulldown) and shows no external clamp in the injector section. Potential savings exist if 20 mH heating is acceptable, but rusEF | [R30.01] Survey wrong: Hellen Miata boards use ZXMS6005SGTA injector drivers, not AUIPS2041L: All four Hellen Miata BOM-replace files swap injector drivers Q305-Q312 to ZXMS6005SGTA (60/65/70 V clamp, 480 mJ, ILIM min 2.2 A at 3 V gate / 3.3 A at 5 V, 150-200 mOhm). The pulse energy (10 mJ, about 1.3 A) is tiny. The limit is the 0.5-0.6 W average power in a smaller SM

title: Charge warning lamp (1Q/3U) never driven and alternator sense/field loop open
statement: Four sources say stock 1Q is the ECU low-side charge/battery lamp output and Haltech shows the alternator has P (feedback to ECU) and D (duty from ECU) wires. The board leaves 1Q and 1T unconnected and ships alternator control off. The dash charge lamp never lights, even at key-on bulb check, so a charging failure goes unnoticed. Whether the alternator charges normally with the ECU loop open is not verified; one forum thread reports a no-charge case. Also reported: [R18.05] Alternator field (1O), generator sense (1T) and charge lamp (1Q) are PCM-driven: Generator connector has D and P; key on D about 0 V and P <1 V; idle P 3-8 V. Lamp is ON key-on, OFF after start via PCM 1Q. Mazda does not say what happens if 1O is undriven; forum says lamp current can seed the field on some alternators (unverified). | [PIN-9900-B.01] Charge warning lamp never works (1Q open): Factory charge lamp is fed from IG and sunk by PCM 1Q (BR/R); the board leaves 1Q (and 1T feedback) unconnected, so the lamp never lights at key-on or on charging failure. The repo lists it as not driven but not the consequence: no warning of a flat or failed  | [PIN-0105-A.03] Generator warning lamp 3U never driven: Stock PCM sinks 3U: lamp lit key-on (bulb check), off when charging, lit on charging DTCs. Here 3U is open: the lamp never lights and a charging failure gives no warning. Hellen NB2 drives 3U.
best_evidence: interconnect.md cur_mb9900 1Q/1T no net; wiki Mazda-Miata-1999 1Q; MSPNP 'Charge Lamp 1Q, Alternator Sense 1T'; Haltech NB1 page alternator P/D; miataturbo thread 89391 (unverified)
suggested_fix: Route a spare low side (e.g. J5-3 OUT_BOOST, on ordered boards also) to 1Q by wire and drive it via GPPWM/Lua. State the charging consequence in the README. Test the alternator with 1O/1T open on a real car before shipping.

title: ESD foam, box size, shielding bags and foam load points
statement: Pink antistatic poly only limits charging of the bag. Uline's pink 8x10 bag is listed 'does not meet MIL-PRF-81705D & E'. Shielding bags (MIL-STD-3010, ANSI/ESD S20.20) block external fields. They cost $0.056 (LCSC 210x240) to $0.57 (Uline 9x12 reclosable). Also reported: [R25.03] ESD pick-and-pluck foam from US stock dominates pack cost: A 24x24x1 in sheet is $15 (6+ cartons $13). At 4 pads of 9x9 per sheet, a top+bottom kit costs about $7.5. Custom die-cut EPE/EVA kits are listed at about $0.2-1.3 per piece with an MOQ of about 100 and need resistance test data. | [R25.02] 9x9x4 in RSC is the right stock box for 25 mm cushioning: Inside 229x229x102 mm leaves 37/33 mm sideways and 33 mm above and below the 154x162x35 stack, enough for 25 mm foam. 10x10x4 and 12x12x4 are larger and heavier for no benefit. | [R25.06] Foam must carry load at standoff points and rim, not on pins: Standard X7R MLCCs crack at 2-3 mm board bend (flex-termination 5-10 mm, vendor claims). The 1.6 mm 154x162 board with a heavy header is the flex risk. Pins under the board and the header latch must not bear load.
best_evidence: Uline S-5891 vs S-2149/S-2509 (fetched 2026-11-16); LCSC C7543868; vendor ESD comparisons (secondary)
suggested_fix: Design the foam cavity to support at HD1-HD4 and rim with pin relief. Ask the layout reviewers to check MLCC placement near holes and edges.

title: JLC assembly cost structure: extended lines, quantity tier, economic limits
statement: Economic PCBA is limited to 2-50 boards (some options 2-30), single-sided placement and a fixed 255 C reflow. 100 boards go to Standard: setup $25.56, stencil $8.21, $1.53 per unique line (92 lines on the DB, $141), fixtures $41.04, packing $0.50+ per board, and edge rails are required. Standard is never cheaper than Economic for the same design (at least $14.93 handling gap). Also reported: [R21.01] Chargeable Extended lines are the main fixed cost: On Economic PCBA each unique non-preferred Extended part costs $3.07 per order. 37 lines on rev0.10 come to $113.59 per order, about $11.4/board at q=10 and $2.3 at q=50. Each line merged away saves $3.07 per order. | [B05.06] JLC assembly cost is small; alternatives save little: Economic PCBA: about $22 fixed per design-order plus $3.07 per extended line (4 on 8995/9697, 5 on 9900/0105) and about $1.3 per board (52 SMT joints, parts about $1.2). Per board about $3.5-3.9 at 10, $2.2 at 25, $1.7 at 50. All-basic substitution saves $12-1 | [B04.08] Design qualifies for JLC economic assembly: All 330 SMD parts are on the top side and the board is 125 x 76 x 1.6 mm, 6 layer, within JLC's stated economic limits (2/4/6 layers, 0.8-1.6 mm, one side of SMT, 2-50 pcs). The BOM has 48 basic, 7 preferred-extended and 38 non-preferred extended lines, so abo
best_evidence: https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-price (2026-10-22); kb/parts_manifest.json jlc_library and jlc_preferred flags
suggested_fix: Consolidate duplicate-function Extended lines (3 BAT54 variants, 3 LED colours, 3 1206 resistor values, ES1D/B360A/SMAJ/SMCJ/1.5SMC lines) and prefer Basic or Preferred parts.

title: Ordered motherboards: F4 0.5 A and no boost flyback diode on AUX header
statement: The ordered J5 is 16 pins. It has no D5 flyback diode on the boost output and no CAN pins. J5-12/13 are PC6/PC7 with a 10k series resistor and a BAT54S, with no pull-up and no RC filter. The frozen firmware does not configure them as flex or nitrous inputs. A flex sensor needs an external 4.7k pull-up to J5-14. Nitrous on PC7 shares EXTI line 7 with HALL1 on PE7, so use it polled. Also reported: [P16.03] Ordered mb F4 (0.5 A) trips with typical boost valve: 0.5 A hold (0.34 A at 60 C, 0.24 A at 85 C) is below the 0.45 A boost valve the install doc cites (unverified) at high duty; current boards use 1.1 A (0.71/0.52 A), which also matches the 0.5 mm AUX_VBAT track. | [B17.05] No boost flyback diode D5 and 0.5 A F4 on all ordered motherboards: Current boards add SS34 D5 from AUX_VBAT to OUT_BOOST and a 1.1 A F4; the ordered boards have neither. A boost solenoid on J5 would rely on the daughterboard driver's own clamp and the 0.5 A PTC, which ABOUT.md says a boost valve mostly uses. This is already i
best_evidence: ord_mb*/pcb_pads.csv F4 1206; INSTALL.md:336; datasheet C70077; 0.5 mm 1 oz track IPC-2221 about 26 C rise at 2.2 A (inferred)
suggested_fix: Document the external pull-up and diode. Set the pins in TunerStudio. Replace F4 with 1 A only after checking the track.

title: Wideband field issues: pinned firmware lacks upstream fixes, USB-only power, heater/supply failures
statement: rusEFI wideband #71 reports the module falling into SensorUnderheat with no way out when the ECU is powered from USB only. The thread's explanation is heater supply 0 V with Force heating set. The issue is still open. A uaEFI wideband that blinked once was a poorly pinned cable. Single units transmit as dual, using CAN IDs 190-193. Also reported: [R02.02] Pinned wideband firmware lacks upstream fixes: The pinned wideband 27e115b (branch prod-2026-01) does not contain upstream commits 9295698 (avoid heating when battery voltage is low, 2026-04-10) and 91aa7c6 (ignore firmware-update request without ID). Issue #348 (stuck underheat after 12 V loss) was filed  | [R02.05] Field failure modes of the module are mostly heater/supply and assembly related: Open or unresolved: 65 s to detect a missing sensor (295), lean blip at start (303), unprotected inputs (a heater wire on Vm destroyed an F042) (309), and ten JLC-built rev B boards reading 1.01 in free air with zero pump current (forum, cause unknown, resembl
best_evidence: work/R02.../master_not_in_pinned_log.txt (41 commits not in the pin); github issue 348 via API
suggested_fix: Keep the sacrificial resistors; check the pump driver and shunt on the first board; add the miswire tests (heater to Vm, battery to Ip) to the bench list.

title: Immobilizer on 2001-05 lights dash lamp; document or switch
statement: AMP states the MSPNP does not handle the OE immobilizer and the dash light flashes. A forum post says the MSPNP-Pro has a jumper to allow or ignore it, and another vendor reportedly emulates it. A no-start with a flashing light will be read as a defective ECU. Also reported: [R19.03] Standalone swap leaves security lamp flashing: MSPNP-Pro MM0105 docs say the dash fault indicator will illuminate or flash. A MiataTurbo thread reports intermittent flashing on a standalone, and owners pull the bulb. No source found for a fuel cut after seconds, and the engine is reported to run. | [R04.03] No immobiliser function on 2001-05 (lamp lit/flashing): The incumbent states it has no OE immobiliser function and the dash fault indicator will illuminate/flash on 2001-05. Buyers learn this only from the manual; the repo lists immobiliser as unsupported, so same gap.
best_evidence: files/R04/manuals_txt/amp-pnp-mm0105-installation.txt (Immobilizer Warning Light section), pro-mm0105, pro-msm0405
suggested_fix: State in the docs and on the product page that the immobilizer is unsupported and what the light does. Test a car with the immobilizer. Consider a bypass or emulation option later.

title: Constant 4 ms dwell without voltage correction or max-dwell guard
statement: Firmware ships constant 4 ms dwell with voltage correction 1.0 over 8-15 V; rusEFI has no max-dwell guard for GPIO-driven igniters. Miata coil packs are reported (forum) to die from over-dwell; spark energy falls at the cranking dip. Also reported: [F02.06] Constant 4 ms dwell with no voltage correction: Dwell is 4 ms constant, voltage correction 1.0 from 8-15 V; at cranking/low battery coils may be under-charged and at 14 V a high-energy coil may overheat. No source for stock NA igniter or NB coil pack dwell was found.
best_evidence: repo/firmware/ext/rusefi/firmware/controllers/algo/defaults/default_ignition.cpp:112-115; grep maxdwell only MC33810 (engine_controller.cpp:599); forum threads miataturbo 96997, 23550
suggested_fix: Ship a voltage-compensated dwell table (draft in notes sec.5, to be scoped) and document scoping dwell before first drive.

title: Wideband F103 blank until first flash; flash step fragile
statement: The flash refuses with the engine turning, erases the wideband settings, and a failed flash leaves the F103 blank (needs retry or SWD pads). The button is a numeric board action in the ini, so a mismatched ini gives the wrong button behaviour. rusEFI's own Update wideband firmware button is the wrong one for this board. Also reported: [F03.03] Blank F103 means no wideband until first flash: A JLC-assembled F103 has empty flash, so the wideband does nothing until the ECU runs and the user presses Flash on-board wideband (or SWD J102 is used). The seller should flash it before shipping and the install guide must say so.
best_evidence: VERIFICATION.md:196-199; board_commands.ini; firmware/README.md 'Flashing the on-board wideband'
suggested_fix: Flash and check wbo_uart_status at the bench; hide or relabel the button for customers.

title: Wideband heater can start without CAN allow and F103 has no watchdog
statement: Heater preheat is 2 V for 5 s then ramps from 7 V, and rusEFI sends allow only when the engine is running (matches Bosch 4.3.2). But with no CAN command the wideband auto-starts from battery voltage, so a CAN fault could heat a cold sensor before engine start (against Bosch). Also reported: [F03.01] Wideband MCU has no watchdog; hang can leave heater on: IWDG is disabled in the port. If the F103 firmware hangs while TIM2_CH3 output is high, the VND14NV04 stays on and drives the LSU heater at full battery voltage (Bosch max 13 V effective). The same is true of upstream firmware.
best_evidence: mcuconf.h:225 STM32_WDG_USE_IWDG FALSE; heater_control.cpp pinned limits only voltage/duty in software; Bosch LSU49 datasheet p2 heater strategy 13 V max
suggested_fix: Enable the IWDG in the port and kick it from the heater thread, so a hang resets the MCU and the R126 pull-down turns the heater off.

title: BAT54WS-7-F replaceable by 7-9x cheaper clones
statement: 11 BAT54WS-7-F cost $0.094 each at qty 50 ($0.084 at 150). Clones with identical VF/IR/CT limits: C7502694 hongjiacheng (EXTENDED+PREFERRED, $0.0107@500, stock 46.9k) and C3040452 Fuxinsemi (EXTENDED, $0.0103@500, stock 73k). Saves about $0.89 per daug
