title: A/C condenser fan 1I/2C not commanded with A/C
statement: Only fan1 (2B, radiator fan) gets fan1AcMode=Relay; fan2 (2C, condenser fan) stays Disabled and comes on only at 95 C. Hellen NB2 sets fan2AcMode=Relay on 2C (named AC Fan). Whether the stock ECU also runs the condenser fan with A/C is not shown by the Mazda tables. Also reported: [PIN-9900-A.02] A/C condenser fan 1I not commanded with A/C (fan2AcMode never set): 1I is the A/C fan relay per wiki, Hellen, MSPNP and Alex. The NB1 preset sets only fan1AcMode=Relay (radiator fan follows A/C). fan2AcMode keeps rusEFI's default Disabled, so the 1I fan runs only above 95 C, not when the A/C is switched on.
best_evidence: repo/firmware/board/miata_board.cpp:228 (only fan1AcMode set); rusEFI fan_control.cpp:289 default fan2AcMode Disabled, :266 fan2OnTemperature 95
suggested_fix: Set engineConfiguration->fan2AcMode = fan_ac_mode_e::Relay in setMiataNb1 (and check how stock behaves). Confirm what 1I switches on a real car.

title: J5 header no pin labels; J5 UART pins mismatch between DB generations
statement: The 20-pin add-on header (COP, boost, alternator, knock, CAN, 5 V, 12 V) has only an outline and a square pin 1 on the silkscreen: no pin functions or pin-1 text. Option parts R20-22/R27/R28/R30/R37 and JP4/JP5 carry only reference names. Also reported: [P18.01] Ordered DB rev0.9 and current motherboards differ on J2.24/25: Ordered DB has UART_TX/UART_RX on J2.24/25, current DB has IN_FLEX/IN_N2O, and every motherboard matches its own generation. Mixing generations connects UART to flex/N2O input lines.
best_evidence: gr_text list of miata_mb_*.kicad_pcb (no J5 text); top_all.png crop of J5
suggested_fix: Mark generations as not interchangeable in docs; never plug ordered DB on current MB (or reverse) without checking.

title: Idle PID clamped to constant 20 percent on NA6/NA94
statement: NA common settings set idleRpmPid.minValue=20 while maxValue stays the default 20, so PID output is clamped to a constant 20 % and the README's closed-loop idle does not exist on 1989-95. The base open-loop curve is rusEFI's generic 75->50 % because the tuned 28->20 % curve is commented todo, so idle may be very high or unstable.
best_evidence: mazda_miata_1_6.cpp idle block; engine_configuration.cpp:524-525,365-371; efi_pid.cpp:114-118; mazda_miata_base_maps.cpp:33-34
suggested_fix: Set idleRpmPid.maxValue (e.g. 40) and use the 28->20 % open-loop curve for NA presets; test on a car.

title: rusEFI LTFT compiled in by default and undocumented
statement: The pinned rusEFI enables long-term fuel trim (a learned trim table that can be applied to VE) by default on stm32f4ems. The board's prepend.txt does not disable it, and the repo docs describe only short-term trim. LTFT adds a TunerStudio page and a separate flash record. Its default switch states and flash-write behaviour on this board are unchecked. A shallow clone of FOME has no LTFT code.
best_evidence: rusefi long_term_fuel_trim.cpp:3-8; efifeatures.h:57 EFI_LTFT_CONTROL TRUE; tunerstudio.template.ini lines ~5328-5333; no LTFT string in repo/firmware/board (grep)
suggested_fix: Decide whether LTFT is shipped. If not, add #define EFI_LTFT_CONTROL FALSE to prepend.txt. If yes, document it and set safe defaults (gathering on, apply off).

title: F407 DFU entry failed with slow 8 MHz crystal; HSE needed
statement: The F407 ROM bootloader waits about 800 us for the HSE. The 8 MHz crystal needed about 900 us, so the bootloader reset. Hellen moved to a 20 MHz crystal. Separately, two assembly batches with the same MCU part number differ in auto-reboot after DFU. Whether this project's crystal avoids the problem was not checked.
best_evidence: https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/79 ; https://github.com/rusefi/hellen-NB2-issues/issues/5 ; https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/4847
suggested_fix: Check the crystal frequency and start-up time in the design. Test DFU entry on every unit, with BOOT button and by software.

title: STM32F407VET6 512 kB cannot run current rusEFI
statement: The current rusEFI F407 image is 640,368 bytes (hellenNA6 release 2026-11-16) and this project's build links to 669 kB. VET6-class 512 kB parts cannot hold it. rusEFI's own VET6 build is a legacy 450K special case with storage and RTC disabled. Only 1 MB (xG) parts qualify.
best_evidence: GitHub release 2026-11-16, hellenNA6_autoupdate.zip bin size; repo/VERIFICATION.md:714; config/boards/STM32F407VET6_Mini.bat
suggested_fix: Do not substitute VET6 variants, including the cheap GD32F407VET6 and APM32F407VET6.

title: Hellen survey wrong: ZXMS6005 injector drivers and STM32F407ZGT7
statement: hellen-miata-NB1 rev c and hellen-miata-NA8 rev A are built with STM32F407ZGT7 (-40..105 C, JLC extended, 34 in stock, USD 27.80@1) against 6.26 for the -6 grade, so 'nobody uses the 105 C grade' is false; the owner's processor decision (VGT6) was justified partly by this claim.
best_evidence: bom_replace_64_NB1-c.csv and bom_replace_64_NA8_96-a.csv line U105; tools/lcsc.py C1337111, C19156
suggested_fix: Fix the survey; re-state the grade decision as cost (about USD 20 per board on the sibling part) vs margin, not as 'everyone does it'.

title: TCAN1042VDRQ1 low stock; TJA1042 pin-identical and cheaper
statement: TCAN1042VDRQ1 has 207 pcs at JLC (extended). NXP TJA1042T/3/1J (C132227) has 62k stock, $0.31@30 / $0.26@100 vs $0.60 / $0.52, extended; SO8 pinout identical (1 TXD,2 GND,3 VCC,4 RXD,5 VIO,6 CANL,7 CANH,8 STB), VIO 2.8-5.5 V, bus +-58 V. Saves ~$0.55/board with no layout change.
best_evidence: NXP TJA1042 Rev.12 Table 4 and limiting values; tools/lcsc.py today; TI SLLSES9C p.4
suggested_fix: Swap C485806 for C132227 on both transceivers (check JLC part-library footprint rotation in preview).

title: 1989-93 fan relay on 1R; README labels for 1L/1M wrong
statement: On the 1991 ECU 1L and 1M are empty; the cooling fan relay is BLK-GRN on 1R (ECU grounds the coil). README calls 1L 'radiator fan relay' and 1M 'vehicle speed sensor' for 1989-93. The real fan output on these cars is the fan2/LS7 output on 1R (JP3 in 90-93 position); firmware fanPin (1L) drives nothing and there is no vehicle-speed signal. The stock thermoswitch still runs the fan independently, so no fan is lost.
best_evidence: 1991 wiring diagram Fig. 2 CONN#1 L, M empty, R BLK-GRN to COOLING FAN RELAY; rusEFI 1990 table 1L/1M N/C, 1R BLK/GRN; README harness table; rusEFI fan_control.cpp:264-266 (fan2 95 C).
suggested_fix: Fix README table (1L/1M unused on 1990-91; 1R is the fan relay); tell users to set the fan on fan2/LS7; confirm 1992-93 and 1989.

title: 2001-02 vs 2003-05 main relay and 4S differ
statement: The 2002 manual shows 3H and 4S unused (relay switched by key); the 2003 manual shows 3H main relay control (B+ key off, <1 V key on) and 4S as IG1 sense. One 2001-05 board must handle both.
best_evidence: files/R19/charm_2002_pcm_voltage_2.png vs charm_2003_pcm_voltage_2.png and _5.png; wiki.rusefi.com Mazda-Miata-2002
suggested_fix: Check the 2001-05 motherboard and firmware for per-year handling of 3H and 4S, and document the jumper or setting.

title: 1H constant B+ and 3K tank level are known
statement: Mazda PID table: B+2 (PCM back-up positive voltage, constant B+) is on 1H; FTL V (fuel tank level) is on 3K; wiring: 1H = G/R from 30 A FUEL INJ fuse, 1A = L/R from ROOM 10 A fuse. Repo labels 1H 'unclear' and 3K 'N/C or fuel gauge, low'. 2K = wire G/O to cluster, DLC and TCM (tach), contradicting Alex Engineering 'unused'.
best_evidence: files/R18/charm1999_pid_terminal_1*.png, _2*, _3*; wiring2000_B1a_top.png, wiring2000_B1a_connector1_table.png (read by eye)
suggested_fix: Update pinouts_9605.md and motherboard docs: 1A and 1H both always-hot B+ (do not drive), 3K tank-level input, 2K tach.

title: NB 2001-05 CKP/CMP/MAF are 3-wire from main relay
statement: CKP, CMP and MAF each have A = main-relay terminal D (switched battery), B = signal to PCM, C = PCM GND 4A. The board must only provide the input pull-up/conditioning and the ground; it must not supply the sensor. CKP air gap is 0.5-1.5 mm.
best_evidence: Mitchell 2005 manual text lines 2986-2990, 3181-3184, 2710-2714; CHARM 2002 CKP inspection page
suggested_fix: Check that the Hall input circuit (1k pull-up to sensor 5 V) still reads correctly when the sensor is powered from 9-16 V main relay output and when 5 V sags in cranking; document that the sensor 12 V comes from the stock harness.

title: Fuel pump driver killed by ST_SIG fuse on Speeduino NA6
statement: On the Speeduino NA6 PNP the ST_SIG fuse must be pulled before first power-up, otherwise the smart-FET fuel-pump driver trips. Two users report a dead pump driver, and a SpeedyEFI review says the owner had to jump the pump. The 1989-95 car's stock wiring has the same hazard. If this project drives that pin, the install guide needs a prominent pre-power step, or the circuit must tolerate the feed.
best_evidence: MX5_PNP.md wiki (fuel pump section); forum t=4583 post #49515; sp_na6.html review 2022-05-10
suggested_fix: Check INSTALL.md and the motherboard against this trap. Add an explicit pull-fuse step with a photo, or make the pin's drive tolerant of a back-fed 12 V.

title: A/C idle-up stalls recurring
statement: About eight forum threads cover stalls with A/C on. The fixes are idle-up delay and duty, min-rpm threshold and PID delay. Summaries say MSPNP lacks true A/C idle-up.
best_evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/great-c-faq-20954/ and related threads (search summary only)
suggested_fix: Wire the A/C request to a dedicated input, enable idle-up in the base maps, and document the settings.

title: J3 Molex C587650 stock 0
statement: The hand-fit IAT header is listed as LCSC C587650 but the manifest, looked up live today, shows stock 0. The owner has to source Molex 43650-0200 elsewhere. The mating plug (43645-0200) is correct for the 43650 single-row header.
best_evidence: kb/parts_manifest.md lines 344, 377, 406, 436, 466
suggested_fix: Order 43650-0200 from a distributor (Digi-Key or Mouser), or use a JST/PH 2-pin header and change the footprint in a later revision.

title: Hole drill 1.1 mm vs TE 1.35 mm
statement: TE drawing 178780 gives PCB mounting holes 76 x dia 1.35 +-0.10 (true position dia 0.2). Repo and Hellen use drill 1.1. With post 0.64 sq (diagonal 0.905) plus 0.2 position tolerance the 1.1 hole has about zero margin, so some posts may not seat. Hellen ships with 1.1, which suggests it is usually workable. Mated-in-place fit not tested.
best_evidence: TE 178780 rev P10 (LCSC C5166246 PDF) mounting dimensions block; TE_178780-1_76P.kicad_mod pad drill 1.1; Hellen P2 drill 1.09982
suggested_fix: Set drill to 1.3-1.35 (pad 1.8 leaves 0.22 annulus) on new boards; on ordered boards test-fit a header and open the holes with a 1.3 drill if needed.

title: Recessed-thread case hole needs 3 M4 washers
statement: The rusEFI wiki states one mounting hole of the NA case has a recessed thread (stock heat sink location) and needs a stack of 3 M4 washers. INSTALL.md says to use the stock screws in six holes and does not mention it; the kit lists no washers.
best_evidence: wiki.rusefi.com/Legacy-Miata-NA-48-pin-board-for-MRE (local work/B13-mechanical-stack-and-case/web/mre_na48.html); repo/INSTALL.md lines 143-161
suggested_fix: Add 3 M4 washers to the kit and a step identifying that hole; check the floor under the screw-head spots.

title: No test points, fiducials; wideband SWD on bottom
statement: The daughterboard has no test points at all. F407 SWD (J3) is on top and usable; F103 wideband SWD (J102) is on the bottom, covered by the motherboard once mated, and the F103 has no USB. DFU on the F407 works only when mated via the motherboard USB-C. A production test needs a bed-of-nails or probes on component pads.
best_evidence: misc.py (no TP refs); pcb_pads.csv J3/J102 rows; kb/interconnect.md J2.30/31 USB
suggested_fix: Add 1 mm TPs for VBAT, +5V, +3V3, GND, NRST and the key I/O, a bottom-accessible or edge SWD for the F103, and have JLC program the chips if the interface is described to them.

title: One-way wiring changes on 1990-93 not flagged irreversible
statement: The optional one-wire-per-injector conversion cuts the stock paired injector joints, and the F/P wire and TPS changes also alter the car. After these, refitting the stock ECU may not run injectors 3 and 4 unless they are re-joined (INFERRED from the stated pairing). The guide does not list the undo steps.
best_evidence: INSTALL.md 'One wire per injector' steps 3-5 and JP1/JP2 explanation.
suggested_fix: Mark these modifications as not reversible with the stock ECU; add undo steps or recommend splice-in connectors.

title: Rev 0.10 F1 1.1 A PTC holds only about 0.52 A at 85 C against 0.45 A cranking load
statement: The datasheet derating table gives 1.10 A hold at 25 C, 0.71 A at 60 C, 0.66 A at 70 C and 0.52 A at 85 C (also the part's operating limit). The logic supply draws about 0.4-0.55 A (the repo says ~0.45 A cranking at 8 V), and F1 sits beside the hot TVS and diode in an enclosure. Margin vanishes above ~70-85 C air at a weak crank, so the 5 V rail could drop out. Also reported: [P06.02] Rev 0.10 F1 1.1 A PTC holds only 0.52 A at 85 C: The rev 0.10 fix (1.1 A hold) derates to 0.52 A at 85 C ambient per the maker's table, against the repo's 0.45 A at 8 V cranking and about 0.6 A at 6 V (constant-power scaling). There is no margin for a hot-soaked case plus a weak crank, and the card adds up t
best_evidence: datasheets/txt/C883150_BSMD1812-110-33V.txt Thermal Derating Chart (85 C: 0.52 A); VERIFICATION.md L684; design.py L212
suggested_fix: Bench hot-soak plus crank test. If it trips, use a higher-hold 33 V 1812 PTC (BSMD1812-160 is 0.63 A at 85 C, little gain) or drop F1 for a 0 ohm link, accepting that an internal short then waits for the car fuse.

title: F407 VDDA and VDD decoupling caps too far from pins
statement: Pins 11,19,28 share C3 at 3.7/5.6/7.8 mm pad-to-pad; pins 6/100 share C1/C2 at 3.5-6.6 mm. Every 3V3 pin goes through a via 2.4 mm away under the package into the In4 plane, so pin-via to cap-via distances are 5.5-9.7 mm. ST says close to or below the pins. Pins 50 and 75 are fine (C5 shares via, C6/C7). Also reported: [B07.01] F407 VDDA/VREF+ filter caps 9-11 mm from pins, none at the pin: Only C11 (1u) and C12 (100n) decouple +3V3A, and they sit at the ferrite FB1, 9.2-9.6 mm pad-to-pad from U1 pins 21/22, routed 9.9-11.3 mm with 2 vias and a B.Cu hop. No cap at the VDDA/VREF+ pins. ST wants them as close as possible to the chip.
best_evidence: pcb_nets.txt /MCU/+3V3A = C11.1 C12.1 FB1.2 U1.21 U1.22; route script d1.py; DS8626 Rev9 p.136 (txt lines 4742, 8061-8065)
suggested_fix: Move C12 (and C11) to the pin side next to U1.21/22 (or add 100n on B.Cu under the pins) with the ferrite upstream. Effect on ADC accuracy is inferred small.

title: J2 JST PUD 3 A contact is thin for LSU heater ramp current
statement: JST rating is 3 A AC/DC at AWG22 including temperature rise, -25..+85 C; heater ramp RMS about 2.2 A (3.9 A at -40 C) with 4.5 A pulses, one contact per heater wire, AEM wire gauge unknown (terminal takes 22-26 AWG). Acceptable but zero margin in hot cabin/cold sensor.
best_evidence: ePUD.pdf p.1 specs; kb/parts/P04 (cold R 3.2 ohm is secondary/unverified)
suggested_fix: Confirm AEM harness wire gauge; keep heater duty-limited at start; consider fast-heating off. Micro-Fit (8.5 A) on ordered boards has no issue.

title: Rotations for TO-252, DSO-8, microSD and others unconfirmed
statement: No community entry exists for these families, and JLC's models were checked only for rev 0.5 parts (README item 2 says J4, the clamp TVSs and the diodes are new and unchecked). The U3/U14 PG-DSO-8 +270 is an extension of the SOIC rule. J4 has no centre offset in JLC_OFFSET.
best_evidence: order_bom.py JLC_ROT/JLC_OFFSET; origin.py: J4 pad-bbox centre -0.55 mm in the footprint y, TO-252 -0.84 mm; notes section 4
suggested_fix: Review these refs in JLC's preview and record the confirmed offsets in JLC_ROT/JLC_OFFSET; check LED cathode marks per LCSC part.

title: Header-in-socket jig soldering; JLC THT placement options
statement: JLC capabilities say THT and mixed SMD+THT assembly is available under Economic and Standard; FAQ prices it at $3.5 hand-soldering per order + per-joint fee (R21 table: $3.58 + $0.0164/joint). The repo hand-fits these parts and marks J1 [self-order], although C592838 is in the JLC library. Also reported: [P18.06] Header-in-socket jig soldering, 160 hand joints per unit: Headers must be soldered while plugged into the MB sockets, so JLC cannot assemble them; hand work is 80 joints on DB plus 80 on MB per unit (JLC THT could do the MB sockets for about $0.05/joint, secondary source). | [R21.11] Seller-fitted J1/J2 headers should stay with the seller: JLC fitting J1/J2 would add $1.67/bd + $0.41 parts at q=10. The repo's self-order BOM says they must be soldered while plugged into the motherboard to come out straight, which JLC cannot do. | [P21.06] JLC stocks S08B-PUDSS-1 (C412098) - could be machine placed: C412098 is extended, stock 10084, $0.36 (1) to $0.20; the repo treats J2 as hand fitted. THT assembly by JLC may save labour.
conflict: JLC can place THT (R22.01, P21.06) versus headers must be soldered plugged in (P18.06, R21.11).
best_evidence: jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-assembly-capabilities (THT FAQ); jlcpcb.com/help/article/pcb-assembly-faqs (wave soldering item); tools/lcsc.py C592838 live: Extended, stock 32, $12.92@1; kb/parts_manifest.md:123 [self-order]
suggested_fix: Test a JLC quote with J1/sockets/MAP as library THT parts (watch preview rotation/footprint); saves seller labour. Stock of J1 (32) limits this to small batches; buy rest from Newark and consign or hand-fit.

title: JLC stock cannot support a 100-board run for TCAN1042, TLS115B0EJ, J1 header C592838
statement: EXTENDED part, stock 554 (JLC) / 554 (LCSC), $1.2617@1, $1.09@30, $0.913@100; two per board gives about 270 boards. Variants C3747428 (D0EJ, stock 45), C540241 (TSON, stock 6) are different parts whose datasheets were not read; TLE4250-2G (C976300, stock 15) is only 50 mA. No basic-part alternative. Also reported: [R21.09] Stock limits for a 100-board run: Live JLC stock for the STM32F407VGT6 is 126, TCAN1042 257 and TLS115B0EJ 556; attrition overage is on top. A 100-board batch would exhaust the MCU stock and needs global sourcing or two lots. | [R22.04] JLC stock limits a 100-unit build for J1 and sockets: JLC's C592838 stock is 32; with the socket and MCU stock from R21 a 100-unit batch cannot be sourced from JLC alone. Newark/Farnell/RS hold stock and a Chinese turnkey house can buy from distributors (NextPCB lists Digikey/Mouser/Newark sources).
best_evidence: tools/lcsc.py C592838 today; kb R21 item 8; R24 stock table; nextpcb.com/pcb-assembly
suggested_fix: Buy headers and sockets from authorised distributors in advance; consign to JLC only if needed (HK warehouse, 2% fee min $10, refundable duty deposit).

title: If Hellen 159 mm outline is adopted, J2 and J4 and header y positions overhang the edge
statement: The x position of the 178780-1 header matches Hellen to 0.01 mm (1A at x=15.99 vs 16.00). Hellen's 1A is at y=21.42 and the repo's is at y=18.13, so the header would move 3.29 mm down. J2's courtyard reaches y=162 and J4 sits at y=157.6, both beyond a 159.0 mm board edge. Also reported: [B11.05] If Hellen outline adopted, J2 and J4 land on the bottom edge: With a 159.0 mm tall outline and parts unmoved, J2 (JST wideband header) pads at y 159.1 are outside and the USB-C shield pads at y 158.7 sit on the edge. They must move up at least 2.5 mm; the daughterboard and all other parts clear the six new holes. | [B12.02] J2 and J4 overhang the corrected bottom edge: With a 159 mm tall outline, J2 (bbox y 148.3-162.0) and J4 (152.8-161.8) extend about 3 mm past the bottom edge; nothing else conflicts with the new corners or holes.
best_evidence: Hellen P2 pad 1 (15.99,21.42) vs repo pad 1A (16.00,18.13); repo footprint courtyard for J2 119..130 x 198.3..212 in file coordinates; scripts/cmp.py
suggested_fix: Move J2/J4 (and anything near) up about 3.5 mm in the layout script, then reroute; the moved header also needs a recheck of the top-left area.

title: Stock-case design: customer must open, cut and supply case; no measured dimensions; no way back
statement: Every hobby vendor (rusEFI, DIY-EFI, Alex Engineering, Speeduino) relies on the customer opening the stock case, removing the PCB and cutting USB/MAP/WB holes. No stock case outline, height or bracket pattern is published for any generation. A Miata Turbo poster found a Speeduino board slightly too tall for the case, and the rusEFI NA board needs a 3 x M4 washer stack at one screw because of a recessed thread. Fit risk for the 154x162 mm board is unmeasured. Also reported: [R28.01] Stock-case design removes the way back to stock: The product needs the customer's stock case opened, the stock board removed and the case cut for USB-C, wideband plug, MAP hose and ribbon header. Return to stock for inspection or resale means refitting the stock board into a holed case. INSTALL.md says only  | [R32.08] Case supply and cutting are hidden in the buying flow: Buyer must open their own ECU case and cut openings for wideband plug, USB-C, MAP hose and ribbon cable, and 1996-2005 fit is unverified; product text says only 'your stock ECU case'. Competitors say no cutting/repinning.
best_evidence: INSTALL.md sec 3 opening table; README.md line 91. AMP page says 'no factory parts will be discarded' and 'reversible'; FOME BMM quick start reuses the factory ECU mounts on the BMM case. rusEFI MRE NA 48-pin wiki uses the same case swap.
suggested_fix: Box-contents section: 'You supply your stock ECU case. Openings must be cut (template in the install guide).' Later offer a case-ready option or prepared case/core only after the outline is measured.

title: Offer own enclosure so stock ECU stays whole; printed shell lacks EMI shield
statement: First 10 units: ship the board with an optional MJF-printed shell (est $20-35 each) and keep own-case reuse as a cheaper choice. At 100: a laser-cut and bent 5052 two-piece shell (est $12-25) or printed (est $12-25). Extruded Hammond 1455T2201 is about $42 plus end plates, so it costs more. An external ECU with adapter harness is about $60-100 more. All of these are estimates and need real quotes. Also reported: [R28.02] Offer own enclosure so the stock ECU stays whole: AMP and BMM ship a complete box (BMM 3D-printed case, USB cable, harnesses) and leave the stock ECU untouched. An own or printed enclosure for this product would give reversibility and remove the case-outline placeholder risk on 1996-2005. Added cost is roughl | [R24.08] Printed shell has no EMI shield and poor heat path: A plastic shell loses the stock aluminium case's shielding and heat spreading. rusEFI's note about a heat sink under one case screw shows the stock case is a heat path, and the repo flags the 1989-93 paired wiring as the hottest case. If a printed shell is use
best_evidence: SendCutSend 5052 benchmarks ($8.38 at 10, $6.45 at 100 for a 9x6.6 in 0.063 in part); DigiKey Hammond 1455T2201 $42.25 (aggregator, June 2026); JLC3DP publishes no per-cm3 rate; UK MJF rate 0.20 GBP/cm3 (not JLC).
suggested_fix: Upload a CAD shell to JLC3DP and JLCCNC for quotes at 10 and 100. Measure the stock cases first. Compare to the BMM 3D-printed case at +$50 for billet.

title: Fulfilment plan: home vs 3PL, staged plan, consignment
statement: Stage 1 (10 units): JLC Economic, headers from Newark, hand fit, DFU flash, home test and pack. Stage 2 (10-30): have JLC fit THT library parts to save labour. Stage 3 (30-100): JLC (100 forces Standard) with second quotes from NextPCB/PCBWay when stock is short. Stage 4 (100+): quote MacroFab/CircuitHub/EU house only if coating, FCT, serialisation or quality escapes justify a premium. Tariff (35% DDP on China PCBA, R21) is the same for all Chinese houses. Also reported: [R22.08] Fulfilment cost: home vs small 3PL vs assembler-ship: Home shipping all-in is about $15-18 domestic (R26) plus 10-20 min labour; a 3PL adds about $2-3.2 pick/pack (survey average 3.20), storage $18-25/pallet/month, receiving $5-15/pallet, setup $250-1000 for about half of providers and monthly minimums, with real | [R22.05] JLC consignment from outside China is costly and one-way: Consigning parts requires shipping to JLC's Hong Kong warehouse, a price review, a refundable duty/VAT deposit (13% VAT on value plus duty), a non-refundable 2% handling fee (min $10), and JLC may resell leftovers only back to the seller.
best_evidence: fulfill.com/3pl-pricing (2026 guide, survey-based); redstagfulfillment.com guide via search; kb R26; pcbway.com/oem/electronics-manufacturing (direct shipping claim)
suggested_fix: Pack at home up to about 100 units; use a 3PL when volume is steady at tens of orders per month; have assemblers ship to you or the 3PL in bulk, not to buyers.

title: TunerStudio paid edition needed for autotune; software costs not stated to customers
statement: VE Analyze Live (autotune) requires the registered TunerStudio. Today's store prices are MS USD 69.95 (sale, normally 79.95) and Ultra USD 99.95 (sale, normally 129.95). MegaLogViewer MS is USD 34.95 and HD USD 49.95. Also reported: [F04.09] Software costs and free alternative not stated to customers: INSTALL says only 'TunerStudio'. EFI Analytics lists TunerStudio MS $89.95 list/$69.95 sale, Ultra $129.95/$99.95 (integrated log viewer, trim analyze), MegaLogViewer HD $69.95/$49.95, MS $49.95/$34.95. rusEFI's wiki recommends its own free rusEFI tuner with b
best_evidence: https://www.efianalytics.com/register/browseProducts.jsp (saved work/R11-tuning-software-workflow/efi_products.html, 2026-11-16); https://www.efianalytics.com/register/license.jsp?appName=TunerStudio+MS; book.pdf p.31
suggested_fix: State the TunerStudio cost in INSTALL. Present free rusEFI tuner plus closed-loop trims as the no-cost path.

title: Seller can pre-flash firmware and wideband to remove riskiest customer steps
statement: The customer path includes DFU (BOOT/RESET), Windows driver traps (old STM DFU driver, ConfigManagerErrorCode=28), a one-time wideband flash through TunerStudio, and the .ini matching. The seller can do the DFU flash and wideband flash at assembly, shipping a unit that connects and runs on first plug-in. rusEFI notes firmware from Oct 2025 to Jan 2026 was fragile during updates with poor power. Also reported: [F04.03] Seller can pre-flash everything and pre-select the year: INSTALL's bench check makes the customer pick the year and flash the wideband; both can be done at the bench by the seller (USB only), since the year-specific motherboard is sold with the order. This removes the wrong-NB2-button no-fuel/no-spark trap and a tun
best_evidence: firmware/README.md:38-43 and wideband flash section; wiki HOWTO-Update-Firmware (page fetch); FOME Software_Flashing-Software-Notes.txt
suggested_fix: Pre-flash main MCU and wideband, press the year, save/ship a .msq, confirm CAN lambda; keep the buttons as service only.

title: Cheaper drivers for low-current channels (NCV8406A, L9826)
statement: IACV, VVT, BOOST and ALT carry about 1 A, and the first three have freewheel diodes. NCV8406ASTT3G (C459816, $0.45 at 100, stock 4875, extended) is pin-compatible in function (1 gate, 2 drain/tab, 3 source) and has a 60-70 V clamp, Ilim 5-9.5 A, Rds 210 mohm at 25 C and 445-520 mohm at 150 C, EAS 110 mJ, RthJA 100 C/W on minimum pad. This saves about $1.37 per channel against $1.82 for the VND7NV04. Conduction heat rises from about 0.12 W to about 0.5 W at 1 A hot. This needs a SOT-223 footprint, a copper recheck and the idle/VVT current confirmed. It is not suitable for the paired 1989-93 injectors (2 A). It was the rev 0.9 part. Also reported: [R08.07] L9826 octal low-side driver could replace the light channels but protection and interface are weaker: ST L9826 (SO-20, SPI, 8 x 450 mA, 1.5 ohm typ and 3 ohm max hot, clamp 45-62 V) costs $1.7313 at 30 (951 in stock) against about $3.46 for 7 ZXMS6004FF plus U12. Only outputs 1 and 2 have current limit and thermal shutdown; outputs 3-8 only have over-current/s
best_evidence: datasheets/extra/NCV8406A_lcsc.txt (max ratings, electrical table); lcsc.py live prices.
suggested_fix: Only if cost pressure justifies a layout respin: fit SOT-223 NCV8406A on Q5-Q8 and keep DPAK VND7NV04 on the injectors. Confirm the real valve currents first.

title: VR conditioner (U9 + passives) removable; serves no supported car
statement: No supported Miata has a VR sensor; the VR inputs reach only AUX header J5 pins 7-10. The 27-part group costs about $0.22 per unit at qty 50, plus about $3 per order for the extended part C7549 (unique to U9, while C19726 stays for D36/D37). It also frees PE12/PE13 and board area. Also reported: [B16.07] VR comparator block serves no supported car: 27 parts (about $0.27 at qty 1, one extended part) condition VR crank/cam signals that reach only AUX header J5-7..10. Every year board maps crank/cam to the hall inputs. Removing the block loses only an optional VR trigger via J5 and frees PE12/PE13 and J2-19
best_evidence: lcsc.py prices 2026-11-16: C7549 $0.073 extended, 5.1k 0805 $0.0055, BAT54S $0.0145, 1n 0805 $0.0082; mb_common.py header map; research/pinouts_9605.md; notes sec.5
suggested_fix: Drop the group from the base build (or DNP-variant) unless custom VR trigger wheels are a sold feature; keep the harness pads on J5 if wanted. This shrinks the board and removes one extended part.

title: MAP sensor MPX5700AP dominant cost and thinly stocked
statement: C90152 costs $27.49 @30 (JLC extended, stock 155) and is hand fitted. MPX4250AP C2802676 and MPX4115AP C3259058 have 0 stock at JLC. MPXHZ6400AC6T1 C511770 (SMD SSOP-8, 20-400 kPa, 1.5 %VFSS = +-5.7 kPa, 12.1 mV/kPa, Vs 4.64-5.36 V) has stock 739 at $10.45 @30 / $9.49 @100 and is what Hellen NA6 uses. It would save about $17 per unit plus hand fitting and has 3x better error, but needs a new footprint and a hose/port arrangement. The HZ datasheet and port size were not read (MPXH6400A Rev 6 was). Also reported: [B05.05] MAP sensor is the dominant cost and thinly stocked: MPX5700AP costs $29.12 each at JLC up to 29 pcs ($27.49 at 30+) with only 155 in stock; it is hand-fitted so it is not in the JLC BOM, and it is about 20x all SMD parts on the board combined.
best_evidence: tools/lcsc.py C90152 C511770 C2802676 today; datasheets/extra/MPXH6400A_rev6_components-ru.pdf Table 1/3; ext/hellen-miata-NA6 .../64_NA6_94-BOM.csv.
suggested_fix: Evaluate C511770 as the default sensor on the next motherboard revision (reuse Hellen's MPXH6400A-SSOP8 land pattern after checking the HZ datasheet); keep a through-hole footprint as an option.

title: Unprotected 5 V sensor outputs destroyed Hellen boards
statement: A customer left the stock non-variable TPS connected on a Hellen NA6. Sensor 5 V shorted to ground and the board was damaged. The reporter wrote there was no circuit protection on any +5 V output. Rev C added a tracker regulator. The README says this project has a protected harness 5 V (U14). Also reported: [R01.06] Unprotected 5 V sensor outputs bricked a Hellen NA6: H64b was bricked on install (TPS 5 V pin suspected shorted); no protection existed on any +5 V output; rusEFI fitted TLS115D0 tracking regulators on all boards (NA6 rev C onward). This project's second TLS115 matches the fix; polyfuse alone was judged insuffic
best_evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/hellenNA6_issues/issues/22 ; https://github.com/andreika-git/hellen-one/issues/119
suggested_fix: Production test: short each sensor 5 V cavity to ground and to +12 V on a sample unit. Install guide: identify and remove stock TPS wiring.

title: Domestic shipping budget and cover/signature
statement: USPS Ground Advantage commercial for <16 oz is 7.33-8.95 USD (zones 1-9), retail 10.05-13.65. Add Signature Confirmation 4.15 and insurance to 399 USD at 6.05, plus a box. All-in about 14-18 USD, i.e. 3.5-4.5% of the price. Also reported: [R26.02] Include 399 USD cover and a signature; 100 USD is included only: USPS includes only 100 USD of cover. Full cover to 399 costs 6.05 (USPS fee table) and Signature Confirmation 4.15 electronic. Without them a loss or porch theft leaves about 299 USD uninsured.
best_evidence: https://pe.usps.com/text/dmm300/Notice123.htm (Notice 123 effective 2026-10-04, includes holiday increase to 2027-01-17); kb/research/files/R26/usps_notice123_2026-10-04.txt
suggested_fix: Quote free domestic shipping in the 399 price. Buy labels via a discounted platform (commercial prices). Re-check after 2027-01-17, when the temporary increase ends.

title: UPS/FedEx dimensional weight not competitive
statement: Rounded up that is 10x10x5 = 500 in3, which is 4 lb at divisor 139. Rounded to nearest it is 405 in3, 3 lb. Actual packed weight is about 1-1.5 lb. USPS applies DIM only above 1,728 in3, so these boxes are weight-priced. Also reported: [R26.03] UPS/FedEx are not competitive for this parcel: At 189 cu in with divisor 139 (secondary), UPS/FedEx bill 2 lb. List 1 lb prices are 12-16 USD (secondary). USPS commercial is 7-9 USD.
best_evidence: UPS/FedEx PDFs returned Access Denied. Aggregator figures: darrigoconsulting, ship.com, branvas
suggested_fix: Default to USPS Ground Advantage for domestic parcels; keep the box at or below 9x9x4 outside; compare UPS/FedEx quotes.

title: Jumper setup JP1/JP2/JP3 on 1989-95 motherboard and shunt count
statement: The seller must set JP3 (FAN2) and JP6 on every 1989-95 board, plus JP4/JP1/JP2 on 1994-95, but the BOM lists 6 shunts as Required and the repo has no per-year assembly sheet. Open JP3 is electrically safe but leaves the A/C or condenser fan relay undriven. R20-R22 pull-ups are car-dependent with no default stated. Also reported: [PIN-9495-B.03] cur_mb8995 94-95 needs JP1/JP2 on SEQ and JP3 in 94-95 position: Default shipped state is 1989-93 (JP1/JP2 open). A 94-95 car left that way has injectors 3 and 4 (2Y/2Z) undriven (two dead cylinders under the sequential preset); JP3 at 90-93 sends fan2 logic to 1R, which is the EGR vent solenoid on 94-95.
best_evidence: README jumper table; FSM code 29 (1R = EGR vent B); interconnect.md JP1/JP2 nets; miata_board.cpp NA94 preset sequential.
suggested_fix: Add a per-year assembly sheet: 1989-93 shunts JP3(90-93) and JP6(AFM) only; 1994-95 JP1,JP2 SEQ, JP3(94-95), JP4, JP6; JP5 open. Say how R20-R22 are decided.

title: Customer exits on edge opposite harness; USB-C strain relief
statement: INSTALL tells the user to leave a cable plugged and run it to the glovebox, but the receptacle sits flush with the board edge and the cable leaves the case through a cut hole with no anchor. Also reported: [B13.03] All customer exits are on the edge opposite the harness: The wideband plug, USB-C, ribbon and MAP hose all leave through the bottom edge, where the stock case has no opening, so the customer must cut 3-4 openings in an aluminium case.
best_evidence: INSTALL.md section 3 table; geom csv J2 (19.45-29.55), J4 (75.5-84.5), U2 body x108.9-136.7
suggested_fix: Option A: move J4 next to J2 (about x 35-40) or use a USB-C panel pigtail so one 16 mm drilled hole plus a grommet serves all. Option B: ship a pre-cut end plate once a case is measured. Option C: exit via the harness window if it has spare width (unknown).

title: AEM 30-3427 patchy availability
statement: On 2026-11-16 onefastshop lists 30-3427 at 35.96 USD out of stock, ships week of Nov 30; iagperformance out of stock (contact for ETA); prices 22-51 USD elsewhere; made in China, single source.
best_evidence: onefastshop.com/products/aem-sensor-harness-for-x-series-wideband-gauge-30-0300-30-0334; iagperformance.com 30-3427 page
suggested_fix: Do not make the product depend on one retail part; name a second lead option.

title: Guided first-start procedure with pass/fail checks
statement: A 10-step procedure with a visible pass/fail check per step: desk check, key-on sensors, bench outputs, trigger check with fuel and ignition off, timing light, first start, idle, logged drive, cold-start mornings, trims. Plus proposed automation: pre-start checklist dialog, auto-reverting fixed-timing and fuel-off modes, per-year bench-test card, support-bundle button.
best_evidence: kb/research/R11-tuning-software-workflow.md section 5; built from book.pdf p.11-25 and FOME HT-First-Start-Safely.txt
suggested_fix: Adopt into INSTALL.md and the in-box card. The auto-revert and checklist features would need firmware work.

title: Drop level shifter U12 (relay)
statement: The Diodes ZXMS6004FF datasheet gives VIH = 3 V min, VIL = 0.7 V max, and Rds 400-600 mohm at VIN = 3 V. The 3.3 V GPIO can therefore drive the relay gates directly (CEL already does in rev 0.10). That removes one TSSOP-24 (about $0.39 at 30) and its wiring. The 10 k pull-downs keep outputs off in reset. The hardware enable gate for these channels is lost.
best_evidence: datasheets/extra/ZXMS6004FF_diodes.txt lines 140-160, 241-255; design.py:268-290
suggested_fix: Drive relay gates from MCU pins through 1 k like CEL, delete U12, keep RN2/RN3 pull-downs; confirm the firmware does not rely on DRV_EN_N for these channels.

title: Option: push-pull stage replaced by open-drain ZXMS plus pull-up
statement: Drive each ZXMS gate directly from the MCU with a 10k pull-UP to +5V. Reset gives Q on, so the line is low and safe. Pull the line up through 1k plus the existing Schottky. Firmware inverts ignition polarity. This removes 2 TC4427, 1 HCT04, 8 1206 resistors and 3 capacitors, saving about $1.1-1.3 per board at qty 100 plus 2 extended parts. Short-to-battery survival is kept (Schottky and ZXMS clamp), and the spark edge becomes a hard pull-down. The drawbacks are a slower, weaker high edge that depends on the igniter's input resistance.
best_evidence: qty-100 prices C20551 $0.476, C131317 about $0.15, C26032/C17901 about $0.003; ZXMS datasheet 3 V gate drive OK (RDS 600 mohm); design.py:297-335
suggested_fix: Only adopt after measuring igniter input data. Also check STM32 FT-pin behaviour with a 5 V pull-up when VDD=0 (not read). The ordered rev 0.9 boards cannot change.

title: Shunt clamp required only because of D40/D41
statement: Worst-case injection into +3V3 through all ordinary input clamps is 19.5 mA (all 17 inputs at 14.4 V) and 40.7 mA (24 V), at most 4.3 mA for a single input, below or comparable to the F103's 20-35 mA always-on load. The wideband pump/Vm clamps D40/D41 inject 0.22-0.43 A (pump 14.4-24 V) and 0.7-1.7 A (Vm until F2 trips). That exceeds any load, so the shunt is needed as drawn. Removing the clamp group (about $0.43/unit at qty 100 plus 2 extended-part fees) is only valid together with removing D40/D41, which exposes U101 and the MCU to a harness short.
best_evidence: pcb_pads.csv R108 47R, R109 10R, R110 62R, R61 4.7k, R27 5.6k/R28 10k, etc.; arithmetic in work/P08-3v3-rail-and-clamp/inj.py; notes section 4; mck1117 reference has no such clamps
suggested_fix: Keep the clamp. For a cost cut, drop it together with D40/D41 only if the owner accepts mck1117's unprotected pump/Vm behaviour. Do not remove it alone.

title: MAF/AFM removal needs IAT splice
statement: Speed-density base tune; removing MAF/AFM requires a GM open-element IAT spliced into the MAF connector (pins 1+6 on 90-93 AFM, 3+4 on 96-97 AMP text) or unplugging MAF; MAP hose is routed through a drilled plug (NA) or grommet (NB); cruise car needs vacuum line cut and teed.
best_evidence: mspnp2-mm9495-v2 'Removing the Vane Air Flow Meter'; amp-pnp-mm9697 'Removing the Mass Air Flow Meter'; pro-mm9093 line 62
suggested_fix: Document these steps and kit a tee/hose, IAT sensor option; verify the board's IAT input handles stock and GM sensors.

title: Wideband signal ground at ECU sensor ground
statement: Erratic wideband readings on an MSPNP were fixed by grounding to the ECU sensor-ground pin (22) with the signal on pin 21. Exhaust leaks near the sensor read lean and mislead tuners. The on-board wideband removes the wiring error but the sensor placement advice stays necessary.
best_evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/mspnp-55/99-mspnp2-wideband-install-82322/ ; https://www.miataturbo.net/megasquirt-18/mspnp2-91-miata-wont-idle-goes-lean-regardless-103709/
suggested_fix: Document the sensor position, weld bung and leak check. If an external wideband is allowed, document the ground.

title: Stock-function matrix per year
statement: Incumbent drives idle (PWM1 IAC), fan 1 on PWM2, A/C relay and A/C request, clutch switch, tach, fuel pump (USA/Europe jumper), O2 select; alternator field PWM3 and VVT HC1 only on 99-05/swaps; VICS solenoid only on 99-00 (Injector I, on above 5500 rpm); manual only, no automatics.
best_evidence: MM9900/MM0105/MM9697/MM9495/MM9093 Aux and ECU-connector images in files/R04/pinouts_img/
suggested_fix: Publish an equivalent per-year table (works / does not work / needs jumper) with the product.

title: Check-engine lamp not driven by incumbent
statement: 2009 vendor post: 'The MSPNP does not control the Check Engine light'; current pinouts list 'CEL (via DFIN1)' whose meaning is unclear. OBD-II 1996+ cars lose dash warnings/smog readiness.
best_evidence: https://www.miataturbo.net/mspnp-55/mspnp-check-engine-light-ca-smog-checks-32709/ (vendor post); files/R04/pinouts_img/MM9900-ECU-Connector-Pinout-768x1005.png
suggested_fix: Decide and document CEL behavior (key-on bulb check, fault light).

title: MAP hose clearance 14 mm
statement: The barb points -x with about 14 mm of free run before J5/F1 force a 90 degree turn to the bottom wall. 3-4 mm ID silicone hose of about 7-8 mm OD kinks well below about 20-30 mm radius (rule of thumb), so the stock turn is likely to kink.
best_evidence: kb/boards/B09 lines 136-141; hose OD and radius are a rule of thumb
suggested_fix: Use a 90 degree silicone elbow on the barb, or rotate U2 so the barb points at the wall/hose exit.

title: INSTALL lacks Bosch sensor mounting rules
statement: Missing Bosch rules: at least 10 deg from horizontal with connector up, 40-60 Nm with high-temp grease, boss 10.5-13 mm stainless, gas under 930 C, hexagon under 600 C, plug under 120 C, cable under 250 C, no silicone sealants, cover sensor when undercoating, heater not before engine start. AEM differs on torque (30 ft-lb) and on vertical mounting.
best_evidence: Bosch Technical Product Information Y 258 E00 015e sections 2.2, 4.3-4.11; aem_30-0300_fae.txt:319-345
suggested_fix: Add a short rules box to INSTALL.md section 6; trust Bosch numbers over AEM's where they differ.

title: INSTALL lacks real photos and case-cut template
statement: AMP pages use per-model photos, a tools list and jump links (Installation, Software, I/O, Jumper Matrix, Rear Options Connector). INSTALL.md uses renders, marks the case step 'Unchecked: nobody has fitted a board to a case yet' and gives only a table of opening centres.
best_evidence: INSTALL.md sec 3; https://ampenginemanagement.com/blogs/amp-pnp-documentation/amp-pnp-mm9900-installation
suggested_fix: After the first install, photograph every year and publish a 1:1 PDF drilling template; split into per-year pages with jump links.

title: INSTALL suggests permanent USB cable; SD logging depends on power order
statement: rusEFI and FOME document that SD logging runs only when the car powers the ECU first. If USB powers it first, the card appears as a USB reader and logging is off, and the card cannot log and be read at once. INSTALL.md suggests leaving a USB-C cable plugged in to the glovebox or console. If a laptop or phone powers USB at key-on, logs may silently not be recorded.
best_evidence: https://wiki.rusefi.com/Logging-Guide (page fetch summary); work/R11-tuning-software-workflow/fome/Basic-Features_Data-Logging.txt; repo/INSTALL.md:163
suggested_fix: Document power-up order for logging. Test it on the first board.

title: Brick recovery needs BOOT button inside case
statement: First flash and DFU recovery need BOOT+RESET on the daughterboard, which sits in the stock case; INSTALL.md lists case openings for J2, USB-C, ribbon and hose, not for the buttons. Normal updates go over OpenBLT without buttons, so a brick should be rare (OpenBLT recovery not verified).
best_evidence: firmware/README.md steps 1-2; INSTALL.md:140-157; wiki HOWTO Update Firmware (DFU only as advanced recovery)
suggested_fix: Pre-flash; document opening the case; consider a pinhole/access hole; offer swap/return service; test that a corrupted app leaves OpenBLT reachable.

title: USB drops under EMI
statement: hellen88bmw (4-layer) showed red FATAL and a USB descriptor failure next to a 3-phase VFD. Proteus lost the TunerStudio link when the engine ran. A USB isolator (ADuM3160) cured it for the reporter and a second forum user, a single post. Maintainers could not reproduce it on the bench.
best_evidence: https://github.com/rusefi/rusefi/issues/4310 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=47554 ; https://www.rusefi.com/forum/viewtopic.php?p=48645
suggested_fix: Support page: use a battery-powered laptop or a USB isolator, keep the cable short. Bench-test USB with a coil firing. Check the USB-C ESD and filter parts in the design.

title: Production test list from field history
statement: The public failure record maps to a per-unit test list: sensor 5 V short, continuity of every hand-fitted connector pin, DFU entry, SD card, wideband heater test, analog input check, USB with the engine on, and ignition outputs low at clock failure. Add a wiring-first-power checklist and a returns policy for ESD and arrival damage, for which I found no public cases.
best_evidence: Case table C1-C33 in kb/research/R31-field-failures-open-ecus.md
suggested_fix: Write the test list into the assembly procedure and keep a fault log per serial number.

title: mpn.json incomplete; bom.py claim false
statement: bom.py says every LCSC number was looked up and nothing is left to flag. mpn.json has no entry for 14 codes the current boards use (C25341, C155605, C95063, C485806, C70065, C131317, C23892, C85085, C916423, C15008, C17901, C17903, C17969, C26032). 44 entries are unused. This is how the R110 error went unnoticed.
best_evidence: set difference of LCSC codes in design.py plus the four mb modules against mpn.json keys: 14 missing, 44 unused. bom.py:7 comment.
suggested_fix: Add a release-time check that compares every BOM LCSC code's value or MPN against the manifest, and regenerate mpn.json from the current BOMs.

title: mb_na8.py dead and would crash
statement: mb_na8.build_parts calls mb_na6.build_parts(HARNESS, paired_injectors=False, ...), but that function has no paired_injectors argument (TypeError). The module still describes the pre-0.12 94-95 wiring (HARN_IAT/JP1). Only mb_make.sh copies it. trigger_select() is defined but never called.
best_evidence: mb_na8.py last line vs mb_na6.py def build_parts(harness=None, idle_pullup=True, tps_links=True); grep shows no importer.
suggested_fix: Delete mb_na8.py and trigger_select, or note that ordered 94-95 boards can no longer be regenerated from the scripts.

title: J4 NPTH pegs 0.194 mm from GND pads
statement: KiCad flags 4 hole_clearance errors (0.194 mm vs the 0.25 mm rule) between the USB-C 0.65 mm NPTH pegs and the outer GND signal pads; it comes from the GCT footprint geometry and is present on the ordered boards too. Likely accepted by JLC, but unconfirmed.
best_evidence: fab_drc_report.txt hole_clearance x4 on 8995, 9697, ord_mb8993
suggested_fix: Confirm in JLC DFM output; accept if no warning.

title: Swap TVS D12/D6 to MDD equivalents
statement: MDD SMCJ30A has the same key specs in its datasheet (VBR 33.3-36.8 V, Vc 48.4 V @31 A, 1500 W, IFSM 200 A, RthJL 15 / RthJA 75 C/W; datasheets/extra/C408374_SMCJ30A_MDD). Stock 7,064, extended, same DO-214AB. Price $0.1303@50, $0.1174@150 vs Littelfuse $0.237@50, $0.211@150, which saves about $0.11 per D6 (D3/D4 too). VF at 100 A not listed on the MDD sheet; brand quality untested. Also reported: [P06.11] Swap D12 SMAJ33A to MDD C113966: MDD SMAJ33A has the same VBR 36.70-40.60 V, Vc 53.3 V @7.5 A and 400 W; its IFSM is 40 A vs 60 A, irrelevant because D12 never conducts forward behind D7/F1. Stock 11,365, extended. Price $0.0331@200 and $0.0416@1 vs Littelfuse $0.1117@50, which saves about $0
best_evidence: tools/lcsc.py C408374 / C224048 today; datasheets/extra/C408374_SMCJ30A_MDD.txt L86-95, L141
suggested_fix: Change C223988 to C113966 on D11/D12 (check D11's forward duty first; it belongs to another review).

title: Optional ferrite and LEDs can use BASIC parts; only one passive replaceable
statement: Extended passives: C17969, C25341, C26032, C106862 plus the 'preferred extended' C23221, C25771, C25917, C36871. R144-R147 (3.3k 1206) could use the basic 4.7k 1206 C17936 ($0.0077@1, 2.08 M stock): 122 mW at 24 V, 44 mW at 14.4 V, but a 1.4x slower pull-down. That removes 1 distinct extended part (4 placements, about $0.003 each, the saving being mostly the extended-part fee). The other six have no safe basic equivalent (the values set the wideband analog and fault-fuse behaviour). After the R110 fix the extended passives still number 8. Also reported: [P22.10] Optional ferrite and LEDs can use BASIC parts: BLM18PG121SN1D (C14709, BASIC, 120 ohm, 2 A at 85 C, DCR 0.05/0.10) replaces the extended BLM18PG221SN1D for VDDA filtering (loads a few mA). Of the status LEDs only red is BASIC. Savings is a per-order setup fee (UNVERIFIED about $3 per extended part type), n
best_evidence: lcsc.py C26032 ext, C17936 basic, C26010 0805 basic (125 mW is too low at 24 V: 175 mW); manifest jlc_preferred flags
suggested_fix: Swap FB1 to C14709 only if the VDDA noise margin is not a concern (220 to 120 ohm at 100 MHz). LEDs not worth changing.

title: F407 needs HSE crystal; wideband crystal optional
statement: F407 datasheet: the USB OTG FS clock is generated by a PLL from the HSE, and the HSI is only +-1% at 25 C and -8/+4.5% over temperature, so Y1 must stay. The wideband F103 HSI is -2/+2.5% over -40..105 C. Upstream f1_rev3 runs the wideband on HSI with no crystal, including CAN. Removing Y101 and its two caps saves about USD 0.20-0.30 per board but costs CAN timing margin and a firmware change (the repo's mcuconf.h uses the crystal deliberately).
best_evidence: datasheets/txt/C12345_STM32F407VGT6.txt:1893 and 6242; C8734 txt lines 3068-3082; ext/wideband-rusefi/firmware/boards/f1_rev3/mcuconf.h:41-50; repo/firmware/wideband/miata_f1/mcuconf.h; kb/parts_manifest.md:18
suggested_fix: Keep both crystals for the first build. Consider dropping Y101 later after a CAN test over temperature.

title: R7 + C16 damper has little effect
statement: The L1/C17-C18 filter has Z0 about 0.43 ohm and Q about 2, so its peak output impedance is about 0.7-0.9 ohm against |Zin| about 10 ohm of the buck at 6 V cranking (Middlebrook margin >10x without a damper). In ngspice the damper changes the ISO 2a buck VIN peak by about 1-1.3 V (38.9 -> 37.6 V). Removal saves about $0.10-0.12 per unit (C16 $0.075-0.121 + R7 $0.003 + two placements). Hellen's module uses the same network (R420 1 ohm + C427 4.7 uF), so it is a proven pattern.
best_evidence: work/P06-power-input-protection/p2a.sh output; ext/hellen-one power_12and5V 0.3 schematic
suggested_fix: Keep for now; if a bench scope shows no ringing at hot-plug and key-on, delete C16/R7 on the next spin.

title: track_current.py never checks INJn_CL nets
statement: The PCB net is '/Outputs/INJ1_CL' but the tool looks for 'INJ1_CL'. It finds no copper and prints '[OK] 0.0 C 0.00 A in 0.0 mm'. The check passes vacuously. Real exposure is small (0.2 A rms on 0.8 mm track).
best_evidence: grep of kicad_pcb: (net 71 "/Outputs/INJ1_CL"); today's run output; evidence/cur_db/pcb_net_routing.csv 0.8 mm
suggested_fix: Match nets by suffix or full name, and make 'no copper found for a loaded net' a CHECK.

title: F103 clone parts save little and differ
statement: JLC alternatives cost USD 0.69-1.04 @1000 against 0.93 for the ST part, saving at most USD 0.15-0.35 each, and CKS32 has only 421 pcs. Reported differences: GD32F103 failed an I2C bench test and has its own system ROM; CKS32 reports SW-DP ID 0x2BA01477; CH32 reads serial number all 0xFF; APM32 and CS32 copy ST's system ROM; internal RC and bus speeds differ. This project flashes the F103 through its ROM bootloader (modelled for ID 0x410) and uses 12 MHz ADC clock and CAN, none of which is tested on a clone. Also reported: [P02.07] Clone F103C8 parts are not worth the saving: C8734 is the genuine ST part at $1.14 @30 / $1.01 @250 with 191k+ stock (Preferred). Clones at JLC (GD32F103C8T6 C77994 about $1.04-1.62, APM32 C393540, CKS32 C556576, CH32 C2687451, FCM32 C3151837 about $0.45-0.91) save at most a few tenths of a dollar, diffe
best_evidence: dl/jlc_search_f103_alts_2052.txt; blaatschaap.be/identifying-32f103-clones; arXiv 2008.09710 via search extraction; repo VERIFICATION.md:351
suggested_fix: Buy genuine ST parts only and do not allow JLC to substitute. If a clone is wanted, bench-test flasher, ADC accuracy and CAN first (APM32F103C8T6 C393540 is the best candidate).

title: Ignition chain (Schottky+FET+74HCT04, Q16-Q19, U13) exceeds proven practice; removable
statement: This saves about $1.7 per board. The low state would then be held only by the 3.3k pull-down, so noise immunity against ground offset is lost. The spark edge also falls at an RC rate instead of being forced. Short-to-battery survival is kept because the Schottky still blocks. Not recommended before measuring igniter input behaviour. Also reported: [R09.05] Schottky+FET+74HCT04 chain exceeds proven practice: No other Miata ECU needs them; simplest proven stage is buffer + series resistor + input pull-down. They protect against coil wire shorted to battery and give a low-impedance falling edge. Removal saves per-channel parts but loses protection; only two channels
best_evidence: Speeduino NA6 TC4424 direct; Hellen ign8 10 ohm; design.py:297-330
suggested_fix: Owner decision; if removed keep 3.3k pull-down and a Schottky-free 100 ohm.

title: U3 second tracker feeds only on-board MAP; removable
statement: U3 only feeds the on-board MAP (7-10 mA) and isolates it from harness faults. Feeding V5_SENS from +5V through the ferrite already used on the BOM (BLM18PG221, C80165) would save $1.09 + caps (about 0.3 % of price) and let MAP work on USB-only power; the extended line stays because U14 remains. Using one tracker for both (Hellen style) exposes the MPX5700AP to short-to-battery. Not worth reworking the ordered rev 0.9. Also reported: [B16.09] U3 (second TLS115 tracker) feeds only the on-board MAP sensor: V5_SENS leaves the daughterboard only to U2, C1 and C2 (MAP sensor) on the motherboard, with no harness wire. Since U14 handles the harness 5 V, U3 ($1.26 at qty 1, extended) could be replaced by a link or ferrite from +5V. Cost: loss of tracker current limiti
best_evidence: MPX5700AP datasheet supply current 7/10 mA; ext/hellen-one power_12and5V 0.3 BOM (single TLS115 U411); lcsc.py price
suggested_fix: Decide for next board revision; keep two if sensor-supply isolation matters more than $1.1.

title: Used donor ECU costs and daughterboard exchange repair
statement: Because the engine logic is on a universal daughterboard, a repair can be handled by posting only the daughterboard instead of the full ECU (INFERRED). That lowers return freight and spares stock. Also reported: [R28.16] Used donor ECU costs for a case or spare: Asking prices for used Miata ECUs appeared at about USD 80-180 (90-93) and 150-250 (99-00). They are undated asking prices, not sold prices. A donor case would keep the customer's own ECU whole.
best_evidence: Search summary of eBay and parts-site listings 2026-11-16.
suggested_fix: If the donor-case route is offered, price it as a customer cost and warn about immobiliser and transmission mismatches.

title: Option: drop F103 crystal Y101 and run from HSI
statement: Upstream rusEFI F1 wideband boards run the CAN at 500 kbit from HSI x12 = 48 MHz with BRP 3. The port could do the same with a firmware config change and the three parts left unfitted, saving about $0.19-0.25 per board plus 3 placements. Trade-off: HSI tolerance versus CAN timing margin, and the author chose HSE on purpose.
best_evidence: upstream f1_rev3 mcuconf.h PLLSRC_HSI, PLLMUL 12; port_shared.cpp CAN BTR identical; Y101 $0.183 @100 (parts manifest)
suggested_fix: Only if bench CAN tests with HSI pass over temperature; set STM32_HSE_ENABLED FALSE, PLLSRC HSI, PLLMUL 12, HSECLK 0 and mark parts DNP.

title: IGN3/IGN4 and BOOST drivers only for optional AUX header
statement: OUT_IGN3, OUT_IGN4 and OUT_BOOST reach no harness cavity on any year. The only exception is boost on 1989-95 via JP6 2-3, an AFM-wire option. The IGN3/4 channels cost about $2.03 and the boost driver about $2.69 at qty 1. Removal loses coil-on-plug on cylinders 3/4 and the boost solenoid output.
best_evidence: map_mb.py (J5 only); mb_na6 JUMPERS JP6; manifest prices C95063 $0.60, C155605 $2.68.
suggested_fix: Consider as a feature-tier decision; fit them only on request.

title: USB ESD part cheap in Blitzbox
statement: Blitzbox uses the ESD0504F 4-channel array ($0.079) on its USB lines, and the NUF2221W1 line on the data lines. The $0.59 USBUF02W6 appears on the project's board class.
best_evidence: Blitzbox BOM, lcsc.py
suggested_fix: Check the project's USB ESD part against ESD0504F (capacitance 0.2 pF, 5 V working).

title: J5 box header has no LCSC code
statement: The current motherboards name an On Shore 302-S201 box header that has to be bought elsewhere. BOOMELE C3405 (2x10, 3 A listed, stock 42.6k, $0.146@1, $0.072@2000) is the 2x10 version of the C3406 2x8 header used on the ordered boards, in the same drawing family (n = 3 to 40). The JLC text for C3406 says '2x5' although the part is 2x8 (params 2x8P).
best_evidence: lcsc.py C3405, C3406; C3406 datasheet drawing '2.54-2xnP, 3<=n<=40', footprint IDC-Header_2x10_P2.54mm_Vertical.
suggested_fix: Name C3405 in the self-order BOM; check the C3405 sheet pin length/height first (I read the C3406 family drawing only).

title: L1 FXL0530 excludes automotive use
statement: cjiang's own spec caution lists 'Transportation equipment (automobiles...)' as not intended; LCSC grade is 'Consumer grade'. The electrical margin is fine (Isat 5.6 min / 7.5 typ A, 29 mohm, 125 C total). Sunlord MWSA0503S-2R2MT C408408 has the same body and identical land pattern and is cheaper, and JLC still lists it, so the repo's 'page not found' reason is not a JLC blocker.
best_evidence: datasheets/txt/C177247 p.2 caution item 8; table FXL0530-2R2-M row; MWSA table row MWSA0503S-2R2MT Isat 7.0 typ, I/J/H = 1.9/2.2/2.5; lcsc.py: C408408 JLC EXT stock 9839 $0.1303@1, $0.1028@50 vs C177247 $0.1537@1, $0.1208@50.
suggested_fix: Prefer C408408 if its stock holds; otherwise keep C177247 (no technical fault found).

title: VND14NV04 has no cheaper equivalent
statement: C2649436 costs $1.36 at 100 (extended, stock 1902). VND7NV04 (C155605, $1.66 at 100) has the same footprint but about 6 A class limiting, so it is neither cheaper nor adequate. A plain logic MOSFET (about $0.10-0.19, e.g. IRLR2905-class) would save about $1.2 per unit but drops current limit, over-temperature and clamp, and a 3.3 V gate is marginal. Its datasheet was not read, so it is not recommended.
best_evidence: tools/lcsc.py lookups 2026-11-16
suggested_fix: Keep VND14NV04 unless the owner analyses a discrete MOSFET with a heater-short strategy.

title: Blitzbox power chain is cheapest observed
statement: Blitzbox protects the supply with a series SS54A Schottky, an SMBJ22A TVS and an LM2940 5 V LDO (85 C max), about $0.4 in total. The LDO has not been checked for thermal margin against this project's load.
best_evidence: blitzbox_v0.1.9_bom_2025-01-08.csv; lcsc.py live
suggested_fix: Use it as a cost benchmark for the current input protection; the thermal check is a separate task.

title: Protected ignition outputs and 5 V gates are project-only
statement: Hellen ign8 is LVC4245 + 10R straight to the igniter; Speeduino is TC4424A + 2.4k. Hellen injector gates are driven from the 3.3 V MCU net. The project's extra protection and 5 V gates are improvements for fault tolerance and Rds(on), at the cost of about a dozen more parts and untested drive timing.
best_evidence: ign8 BOM (10R x8, U460 LVC4245); output module schematic; daughterboard README rev 0.8
suggested_fix: Optional: assess if the extra parts are worth it for the ignition path.

title: 6-layer vs 4-layer is a small cost lever
statement: Going 6L to 4L saves about $3.4/board at q=10 and $2.4 at q=50 (UNVERIFIED PCB estimates). Assembly and parts do not change. 6L also forces ENIG, which is fine.
best_evidence: model.py A10; 6-layer page
suggested_fix: Quote both stackups; keep 6L if the routing needs it.
